title: Quantum Error Correction via Topological Qubits in Simulated Networks
abstract: This paper explores the potential of simulating topological qubits within computer networks as a viable strategy for quantum error correction (QEC). The core argument presented is that simulating topological qubits provides a scalable pathway to QEC, circumventing the significant challenges associated with the physical fabrication and maintenance of actual topological qubits. The work details the development of a network simulation environment designed to implement the fundamental principles of topological QEC. Specifically, it focuses on designing and testing encoding and decoding schemes for a simulated topological code. The research represents a computationally feasible approach to QEC prior to the realization of practical topological qubits, offering a valuable tool for theoretical exploration and algorithm development within the field of quantum computing. The simulation framework allows for investigating complex error dynamics and optimizing correction protocols in a controlled environment, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of topological QEC and its potential for future implementation.

title: Non-linear Topological Self-Organization Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear topological self-organization learning method. Traditional learning approaches often rely on static models, limiting our ability to accurately represent and predict complex system behavior. Our method leverages a self-adaptive algorithm to learn the underlying topology of the system, enabling precise modeling and prediction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations, showcasing improved performance in scenarios requiring detailed system understanding. The core mechanism centers on iteratively refining the system's topological structure, fostering a dynamic and adaptive representation. The resulting system exhibits enhanced robustness and predictive capabilities, representing a significant advancement in the field of self-organization learning.

title: Quantum State Vector Conjugate Matrix
abstract: Quantum state vector conjugate matrix represents a fundamental concept in quantum mechanics, offering a powerful tool for simplifying calculations and optimizing quantum algorithms. This paper explores the design and application of a novel computational model based on this matrix, aiming to enhance efficiency in the computation of quantum state vector eigenvalues. We detail the core mechanism of utilizing the matrix's properties for streamlined calculations, and present initial results demonstrating its potential for quantum algorithm improvement. The goal is to establish a robust and efficient framework for analyzing and manipulating quantum state vectors, providing a significant step towards practical quantum computing.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Metric Spaces for Complex Data Correlation
abstract: This paper introduces Self-Organizing Metric Spaces (SOMs) as a novel framework for analyzing complex data correlations. Traditional correlation methods often assume data independence, failing to capture the inherent relationships that drive meaningful patterns. We propose a new SOM architecture that dynamically structures the metric space based on the data's underlying dependencies, resulting in more accurate and robust data clustering and analysis. The core mechanism involves representing data relationships through a graph-theoretic approach, ensuring that the metric space naturally reflects patterns of similarity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our SOMs through several case studies, showcasing improved clustering accuracy and resilience to noise compared to existing correlation techniques. This work offers a fundamentally different perspective on data analysis, providing a robust and adaptable tool for complex data manipulation.

title: Probabilistic Graph Embedding with Adaptive Clustering
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic graph embedding method designed to generate robust and adaptable graph embeddings. Traditional graph embedding techniques often rely on fixed clustering algorithms, which can struggle with complex graph structures. We introduce a dynamic clustering algorithm that intelligently adjusts the number of clusters based on the graph's inherent complexity, enhancing the reliability of the resulting embeddings. The method leverages probabilistic density estimation to provide a more nuanced representation of the graph's structure. This approach significantly improves the accuracy of graph embeddings, particularly for graphs exhibiting intricate relationships. The research addresses the limitations of existing methods by offering a flexible and adaptive approach to clustering.

title: Dynamic Topology Matrices for Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology matrices, designed to address the challenges of complex optimization problems that exhibit dynamic data distributions. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameters, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving data patterns. The core mechanism involves introducing a "topology layer" that dynamically adjusts the structure of the data space, allowing the algorithm to effectively navigate complex landscapes and converge to optimal solutions. The proposed algorithm offers improved efficiency and precision compared to static optimization techniques by embracing adaptability.

title: Préparer les réseaux de télécommunications à l’ère du quantique
abstract: L’essor des technologies quantiques ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour les télécommunications, mais fait aussi émerger un risque majeur pour la sécurité numérique : la possibilité, à terme, de fragiliser certains mécanismes cryptographiques aujourd’hui largement utilisés. Pour un opérateur comme Orange, cette menace impose une préparation structurée. Dans l’article, nous montrons comment Orange anticipe ce basculement à travers deux axes complémentaires : la migration vers la cryptographie post-quantique, socle de la transition quantum-safe ; et la mise en œuvre de communications quantiques, notamment la QKD, pour renforcer certains liens critiques. Nous présentons les travaux de recherche, les expérimentations européennes et nationales, ainsi que les premières offres destinées à accompagner les clients vers des réseaux plus sûrs et plus résilients.

title: Разработка СХ-платформы для многомерной квантификации потребительского отклика в банковской сфере на основе больших языковых моделей
abstract: Целью работы является разработка CX-платформы, обеспечивающей сбор, обработку, интерпретацию и визуализацию отзывов клиентов Т-Банка, а также формирование системы интегральных показателей и LLM-ориентированных рекомендаций для поддержки управленческих решений. В работе использованы методы статистического анализа, интеллектуального анализа текстовых данных, тематической и тональной интерпретации отзывов, построения интегральных индексов, а также технологии больших языковых моделей и веб-ориентированного проектирования аналитических систем. В результате работы сформирован корпус отзывов Т-Банка с платформы Banki.ru, разработана архитектура CX-платформы, определен состав аналитических признаков клиентского отклика, предложена система интегральных индексов, включающая индекс проблемности, индекс репутационного риска и индекс эффективности ответа, а также реализован LLM-модуль для генерации автоматизированных ответов и управленческих рекомендаций. Практическим результатом исследования стала веб-платформа CX Pulse, обеспечивающая фильтрацию отзывов, визуализацию ключевых метрик, анализ проблемных зон клиентского опыта и поддержку принятия решений на основе отзывов клиентов. Полученные результаты могут быть использованы в задачах CX-аналитики, мониторинга клиентского опыта, совершенствования банковских продуктов и развития цифровых сервисов. Сделан вывод о том, что публичные отзывы клиентов могут выступать основой для построения веб-ориентированной аналитической системы, сочетающей методы статистики, текстовой аналитики и большие языковые модели.

title: A Roadmap for MEG Foundation Models
abstract: Foundation models are beginning to reshape brain-signal analysis by moving the field beyond task-specific decoding pipelines toward reusable models pretrained on broad neural datasets. Magnetoencephalography (MEG) is a compelling but still underdeveloped target for this shift: it captures human cortical dynamics at millisecond resolution while offering stronger spatial interpretability than EEG, making it especially valuable for source-resolved studies of perception, language, cognition, and clinical brain function. Yet MEG foundation models remain at an early stage, with only a small number of MEG-specific and MEG-inclusive multi-modal models, modest pretraining corpora, and emerging but still limited benchmarks. This perspective lays down the basic concepts needed to understand MEG foundation models and provides a didactic overview of the field's key design choices, including tokenization, sensor- versus source-space representations, sensor-geometry encoding, backbone architectures, self-supervised objectives, and pretraining data. We then offer a roadmap for future development, organized around native MEG pretraining, adaptation of EEG foundation models, transfer from generic time-series models, and multi-modal integration with EEG, fMRI, MRI, behaviour, and stimulus features. We highlight the need for coordinated infrastructure, including diverse and reusable MEG datasets, rigorous evaluation across subjects, sites, tasks, and clinical settings, and responsible data-sharing practices that address consent, privacy, access, and governance.

title: Brain2Speech-Net: Fast and Intelligible Brain-to-Speech Synthesis Without Text Decoding
abstract: The loss of speech limits communication for individuals with paralysis. Direct neural-to-speech synthesis is challenging due to the limited availability of neural data for training speech brain-computer interfaces. Most existing systems rely on cascaded neural-to-text-to-speech pipelines, which increase inference latency and propagate errors across stages. We present Brain2Speech-Net, a single-stage neural-to-speech generation framework without intermediate text decoding. We use a differentiable phoneme bottleneck and a deep-HMM alignment mechanism to map long neural recordings into the latent space of a text-to-speech (TTS) model, enabling high-quality speech synthesis. Brain2Speech-Net is the only system in our comparison that produces intelligible speech while generating faster than real time.

title: Conditioning Degenerate Diffusion Models
abstract: Current conditioned generative models heavily rely on score functions for guidance during training. When the generative model is a diffusion process with a singular diffusion coefficient and the underlying (conditional) densities either do not exist or are not smooth, we use causal optimal transport to define \emph{approximate} loss functions that identify a minimum-entropy control for guidance under minimal assumptions. Our approach relies on causal optimal transport and its characterization through the predictable representation property of (conditioned) diffusion processes whose associated martingale problem is well posed, à la Üstünel.

title: Heralded one-, two- and three-photon states from waveguided parametric down-conversion
abstract: The manifold coincidences and singles counting provides a resource-saving quantum-optics analysis tool, since it is appropriate even in the presence of heavy experimental imperfections. Here, we prepare cross-polarized twin beams in the telecommunication wavelength range via parametric down-conversion in a periodically-poled KTiOPO$_4$ waveguide and herald photon-number states up to three photons. First, we show that the single-click probability is a versatile tool not only for extracting the state's mean photon number but also for sampling values of the moment generating function being the core behind any quantum optical state. Second, we measure values of the normalized factorial moments of photon number, $g^{(m)}_{\text{h}}$, up to the order $m = n+1$ for the heralded $n$-photon state. These normalized photon correlations provide an expedient method for examining the higher-order non-classicality of light by violating the condition $g^{(m+1)}_{\text{h}} \ge g^{(m)}_{\text{h}} \ge 1$.

title: Multilingual Agent System for Inclusive Wildfire Evacuation Guidance
abstract: Wildfire seasons have become 84 days longer in the current days than in the 1970s, causing enormous threats to one's financial status and short- and long-term health. During the fire, public agencies send out emergency messages to provide warnings and orders. Although 26 million people in the US have limited English proficiency, over 80% of those messages are only delivered in English, which can cause disproportionate information distribution and awareness. In order to better serve marginalized communities during emergencies, the authors developed BEACON, a service that provides comprehensive and personalized evacuation guidance, including navigation routes, personalized checklists, and a chatbot in the language that a user uses. Our current system ingests data including fire perimeter information, evacuation order status, and shelter information from Watch Duty. When a user is within a certain proximity from the fire, the system utilizes real-time GPS locations and nearby weather data from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to predict fire danger levels. The assessment model refreshment are dynamically scheduled based on fire progress and trends using XGBoost. If the location has a likelihood of fire danger, the system sends alerts with evacuation routes outputted from a polygon-avoidant routing pipeline. The application provides a context-aware multilingual agent that users can communicate with and is tightly connected to other features of the application. In addition, based on data that the user entered, the system dynamically generates and checks off personalized reminder items to provide an organized evacuation plan. The system's user interface dynamically changes its language settings based on the language the user most recently used in either setting or chatbot conversation for all the application elements.

title: Title: Non-Linear Geometric Topology for Quantum Entanglement Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear geometric topology to quantum entanglement simulation, exploring its potential to provide a novel framework for understanding and manipulating quantum states. We propose a dynamically constructed topological structure as a core element, allowing for the simulation of entangled states through the manipulation of this structure. The core mechanism centers around encoding and controlling quantum states using the topology, offering a departure from traditional approaches and potentially revealing deeper properties of entanglement. This research aims to identify potential applications within the realm of quantum computation, leveraging the unique characteristics of topological data analysis. The study will detail the construction of a flexible topology, the implementation of a computational model, and the simulation of entangled states based on this framework.

title: Title: Adaptive Constraint Relaxation for Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents an innovative adaptive constraint relaxation strategy for genetic algorithms, designed to overcome a significant limitation of traditional GA implementations: the reliance on fixed relaxation rates. Conventional GA designs often struggle with premature convergence and suboptimal solutions due to a lack of dynamic adjustment to the population's progress. Our approach introduces a novel monitoring mechanism that dynamically adjusts relaxation steps based on the *evolutionary trajectory* of the solution population, effectively optimizing the search process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through extensive simulations and analysis, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to baseline GA algorithms. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that constantly assesses the population's progress and modulates the relaxation rate to encourage rapid convergence, while simultaneously mitigating premature convergence. The resulting algorithm exhibits improved performance across a range of problem instances, offering a more robust and efficient approach to genetic algorithm design.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Feedback Loops for Control Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive quantum feedback loops to control systems, aiming to enhance responsiveness and improve performance through instantaneous feedback. Traditional control systems often suffer from limitations in speed and accuracy due to delayed feedback mechanisms. We propose a novel approach that utilizes quantum-enhanced measurement to dynamically adjust control parameters based on the system's instantaneous state, fostering a more responsive and accurate system. This research investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of this algorithmic approach, focusing on the core mechanism of utilizing quantum measurement for immediate parameter adjustments. The paper details the design of the adaptive loop, its mathematical formulation, and preliminary results demonstrating improved responsiveness compared to traditional methods.

abstract: Linear Scaling Theory (LST) offers a novel approach to reinforcement learning by incorporating a fundamental mathematical framework that emphasizes the relationship between the system's parameters and the optimization process. This paper explores the application of LST to parameterization optimization within complex systems, aiming to enhance the algorithm's generalization capabilities. We propose a new algorithm that leverages LST to dynamically adjust parameters, fostering a more robust and adaptable system. This work represents a significant step toward developing more efficient and versatile reinforcement learning algorithms, particularly for intricate and dynamic environments.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Graph Completion with Contrastive Predictive Coding
abstract: Graph completion is a fundamental problem in various domains, including social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and computer vision. Traditional approaches often rely on explicit supervision or complex, task-specific architectures. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers an attractive alternative by leveraging unlabeled graph data to learn effective representations. However, existing SSL methods for graph completion frequently struggle to capture the intricate, long-range dependencies inherent in graph structures. This paper introduces a novel approach that addresses this limitation by integrating contrastive predictive coding (CPC) within a graph convolutional network (GCN). The core idea is to train the GCN to predict future nodes or edges given their surrounding context, thereby learning robust representations that explicitly model and capture these long-range dependencies. We formulate the graph completion task as a prediction problem, where the network learns to reconstruct missing edges or nodes based on observed connections. The CPC mechanism acts as a powerful regularizer, encouraging the network to learn representations that are sensitive to contextual information and resistant to noise. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and, crucially, by outlining a practical implementation strategy that can be readily adapted to different graph datasets and completion scenarios. The key contribution lies in combining the inductive bias of SSL with the predictive power of CPC, leading to significant improvements in graph completion performance compared to existing methods.

title: Based on Quantum Decoherence: Distributed Machine Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed machine learning leveraging the unique properties of quantum decoherence. The core idea is to utilize the controllable rate of decoherence in quantum systems to facilitate information exchange and learning between distributed nodes. This allows for the construction of an algorithm that, under specific conditions, can converge towards a global optimum. Unlike traditional distributed machine learning methods reliant on classical information, this approach incorporates quantum mechanics, potentially leading to significant improvements in learning efficiency. The algorithm hinges on carefully managing decoherence, treating it not as a detrimental effect but as a mechanism for controlled information transfer. We present a theoretical framework for this method, detailing the mathematical formalism and outlining the key steps involved in the distributed learning process. The presented method aims to address the limitations of current distributed learning approaches, particularly in scenarios involving large datasets and complex models, by harnessing the inherent parallelism and potential for quantum speedup. Further research will focus on practical implementation challenges and exploring the algorithm's performance across various network topologies and machine learning tasks.

title: Evolutionary Algorithm-Driven Hardware Circuit Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to the optimization of hardware circuit design. The core premise is that EAs, with their inherent ability to explore complex solution spaces and escape local optima, can outperform traditional, manually-driven circuit design methodologies. Specifically, we present a framework where a hardware circuit is treated as a population of potential designs. A genetic algorithm is then employed to iteratively refine this population, focusing on optimizing key metrics such as performance (measured in terms of speed and throughput) and power consumption. The algorithm operates through a combination of circuit topology changes, component selection, and parameter adjustments. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through a theoretical analysis and a conceptual design exploration, highlighting the potential for significantly improved circuit characteristics. This work contributes to a paradigm shift in circuit design, leveraging the strengths of AI-based optimization techniques to create more efficient and effective hardware.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Adaptive Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. Its potential for manipulating and measuring states beyond classical understanding has spurred significant research into its applications, particularly in optimization problems. This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to a novel adaptive algorithm designed to optimize complex machine learning models, specifically addressing the challenge of dynamic data adaptation and improved generalization. We propose a framework utilizing entangled parameters to dynamically adjust model parameters based on input data shifts, demonstrating a significant improvement over traditional optimization techniques in this context. The core mechanism centers around leveraging the inherent, self-organizing properties of entangled states to facilitate continuous parameter refinement and enhanced model robustness. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, the underlying quantum principles, and preliminary experimental results showcasing its efficacy in optimizing a specific, complex machine learning model. We conclude with a discussion of the potential implications and future research directions.

title: Multi-Modal Data Fusion Causal Inference (MDFCI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal inference leveraging multi-modal data fusion. The core idea is to effectively integrate information from diverse data sources – represented as modalities – to enhance the accuracy and robustness of causal reasoning. We propose a framework built upon Bayesian Networks and Structural Causal Models (SCMs), enabling the fusion of heterogeneous data while explicitly modeling causal relationships. The methodology utilizes probabilistic inference to determine the underlying causal structure, accounting for potential confounding variables. This work addresses the limitations of traditional causal inference methods that often rely on single data sources or make strong assumptions about data independence. The resulting model provides a more nuanced understanding of causal mechanisms, particularly in complex scenarios where multiple data streams offer complementary perspectives. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical framework and outline key considerations for its practical implementation. The primary contribution lies in the systematic integration of multi-modal data with a rigorous causal inference framework.

abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive variable space learning framework that automatically adjusts the parameters of a variable space to improve the generalization and efficiency of machine learning models. Traditional variable space learning methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to diverse datasets. Our proposed framework utilizes dynamic parameter adjustment driven by data characteristics, resulting in enhanced performance. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments evaluating various machine learning tasks. The core claim is that this framework enables significantly improved generalization and efficiency compared to existing methods.

title: Quantum Error Correction Based Distributed Storage System
abstract: This paper investigates the design and implementation of a distributed storage system leveraging quantum error correction (QEC) techniques. Traditional distributed storage systems face significant challenges in maintaining data integrity when confronted with high error rates, particularly in environments susceptible to quantum noise. This research proposes a system architecture that encodes data into quantum states and employs QEC codes to provide robust error correction, thereby achieving high fault tolerance. The core claim is the utilization of QEC to realize a high-tolerance distributed storage system. The core mechanism involves encoding data into quantum states and utilizing quantum error correction codes for error protection, enabling reliable storage and transmission. The novelty lies in addressing the reliability issues inherent in conventional distributed storage systems within error-prone conditions. This work outlines the fundamental principles, key components, and potential challenges associated with such a system, offering a pathway toward resilient quantum data storage.

title: Causal Discovery via Graph Laplacian Eigenmaps with Contrastive Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to causal discovery utilizing Graph Laplacian Eigenmaps in conjunction with contrastive learning. Traditional causal discovery methods often falter when dealing with high-dimensional data and intricate relationships, frequently relying on assumptions that are difficult to validate. Our method addresses this challenge by simultaneously leveraging both the structural characteristics of a graph and the statistical similarities between nodes. Specifically, contrastive learning is employed to create robust node embeddings, while Graph Laplacian Eigenmaps encode the graph's topology. The integration of these two techniques provides a more reliable and accurate framework for identifying causal connections. The core innovation lies in the synergistic combination of graph-based structural information and statistical similarity, offering an improved solution for causal discovery in complex systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline potential applications, highlighting its advantages over existing methods.

title: Adaptive Context-Aware Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program synthesis, termed Adaptive Context-Aware Program Synthesis (ACAPS). The core idea is to leverage contextual information – encompassing data flow, control flow, and environmental state – to dynamically generate program fragments that are optimally suited to the current situation. Unlike traditional static template-matching techniques, ACAPS employs reinforcement learning to train a "context-aware" synthesizer. This synthesizer learns a policy to generate code based on the observed program context, continuously refining its strategy for improved efficiency and robustness. We demonstrate the potential of this approach by focusing on the underlying mechanism, detailing the reinforcement learning framework and the contextual representation used. The goal is to move beyond rigid, pre-defined code structures and enable truly adaptive program generation, significantly enhancing the quality and applicability of automatically generated code.

title: 基于动态的神经网络的自适应学习框架
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic neural network learning framework that adapts the network's parameters based on the learning process's inherent noise and uncertainty. Traditional neural network training often relies on static optimization, failing to fully leverage the complexities of the learning process. Our proposed framework dynamically adjusts network weights and biases to enhance learning efficiency and robustness. This is a significant departure from conventional approaches, offering a more adaptive and potentially superior learning strategy.

title: THE QAOA SPAN AS A LAYER-ORDERED KRYLOV SPACE: SUBSPACE DIAGONALIZATION AND NUMERICAL COST
abstract: Combinatorial optimization is often recast as ground-state search for a diagonalHamiltonian, with variational circuits used to explore low-energy states. We askwhich linear trial space is generated by the full depth-$p$ QAOA family and what itcosts to use that space in a projected eigensolver. For independentlyparameterized layers, we prove that the span on every nonempty open angle set equalsthe layer-ordered alternating closure generated by the cost and mixer spectralprojectors. Ground-space overlap then guarantees exact Rayleigh--Ritz recovery ofthe ground value. We realize this construction through finite coordinates, projected-matrixestimation, regularization, eigensolution, and configuration readout. On four smallMaxCut instances with $R=M=90$, coefficient-guided sampling returns an optimum withprobability $0.728$--$1.000$; it outperforms round robin on three instances and islower on $C_{10}$. Under the independent-entry Hadamard-test model, alternatingbases reach majority Ritz-value recovery at$8.1\cdot10^{13}$--$3.7\cdot10^{14}$ shots on three instances, while $C_{10}$remains unreached. For cost-only bases, shared sampling reduces these counts byfive to twelve orders of magnitude, but the resulting Ritz value is bounded belowby the lowest energy already observed. The experiments identify coordinatesensitivity, projected-matrix access, and configuration extraction as the maincosts of exploiting the exact span.

title: High-Dimensional Quantum State Computation Paradigm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computation paradigm, termed the "High-Dimensional Quantum State Computation Paradigm," designed to effectively address the challenges posed by high-dimensional quantum states. Traditional quantum algorithms often fail to fully exploit the potential of non-linear operations in manipulating these states. This work proposes a new approach that leverages specific quantum circuit designs and optimization techniques to enhance the computational power and efficiency of solving problems involving high-dimensional quantum systems. We present a detailed model and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this paradigm in a specific, complex quantum state problem. The core mechanism centers around the strategic application of non-linear quantum gates to effectively explore the state space of high-dimensional quantum systems. This approach provides a significant advancement in the ability to tackle problems that are currently intractable for existing quantum algorithms.

title: Passer à l’échelle : Le calcul quantique à base de circuits supraconducteurs
abstract: Les circuits supraconducteurs constituent une des plates-formes matérielles les plus prometteuses du calcul quantique. Ils équipent les processeurs de Google, d’IBM, d’Amazon et de la start-up française Alice & Bob. La première génération d’ordinateurs quantiques, les processeurs NISQ ( noisy intermediate-scale quantum ), sans correction d’erreurs, ont démontré un fonctionnement cohérent et l’exécution d’algorithmes à petite échelle, mais les erreurs accumulées bornent la profondeur des calculs utiles. Malheureusement, construire une machine tolérante aux erreurs exige des centaines de milliers, voire des millions de qubits physiques, soit quatre ordres de grandeur au-delà des prototypes actuels. Passer à l’échelle, en 2026, est donc un problème d’ingénierie à cinq dimensions : cryogénie ; câblage ; électronique de contrôle ; décodage des erreurs en temps réel ; et fabrication reproductible des puces. Les architectures économes, comme le qubit de chat, peuvent réduire d’un ordre de grandeur la facture matérielle, et rendre crédibles les premières machines utiles d’ici la fin de la décennie.

title: Fusion color space analysis of tongue image characteristics in different stages of metastatic colorectal cancer and three-class model construction
abstract: Objective Color spaces were used to analyze the color characteristics of tongue image in different stages of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), and a three-class model was constructed to predict the different tongue characteristics during the mCRC progression. Methods Tongue images of CRC patients were collected and classified into non-metastatic, oligometastatic, and extensive metastatic groups according to tumor metastasis. The color components in HSB, Lab, and YCrCb color spaces were measured from tongue images and the differences in color characteristics were quantitatively analyzed. Based on the modified YOLO and combined with the expert model and multilayer perceptron (MLP) fusion framework, the three classification models of tongue images were constructed. Results Most of the quantitative results showed the quantitative results for oligometastasis were the smallest values among the three metastatic stages. The S* and b* values at the edge of the tongue and the b* values in the middle of the tongue showed the quantitative results for oligometastasis were the highest values in the three stages. Besides, Cr* values at the edge of the tongue and S* values in the middle of the tongue showed a decreasing trend. In addition, all expert models constructed in the study demonstrated stable convergence on the training corpus within 100 epochs. The overall accuracy of the fused MLP classifier for tongue characteristics classification was 83.3%. Conclusions In this study, tongue feature variations across different stages of CRC were successfully analyzed. A well-performing three-classification tongue image analysis model based on the YOLO architecture was initially constructed.

title: On-board ML for Trace Gas detection in Imaging Spectroscopy data
abstract: Data collected during aerial and spaceborne imaging spectroscopy campaigns enables the detection of transient events such as trace gas emissions. However, current processing pipelines depend on slow, on-the-ground processing, which delays the time to information of each detected event and prohibits immediate follow-up actions. During the Tokyo Field Campaign of March 2026, we explored on-board processing of Imaging Spectroscopy data from the equipped AVIRIS-5 sensor. Due to communication bottlenecks, full datacubes cannot be downlinked immediately during the flight. Instead we downlink the potential events predicted by our efficient and small machine learning model. We show the first on-board detection of methane point source emission with Imaging Spectroscopy data using Edge ML.

title: Efficient Semantic Understanding from Digital Foveation
abstract: Dense semantic segmentation allocates computational resources uniformly across the entire image, regardless of scene complexity or task relevance. Inspired by biological vision, we investigate whether semantic understanding can be achieved more efficiently through digital foveated perception. We introduce a lightweight active-vision pipeline that combines saliency-driven fixation selection, high-resolution foveal observations, low-resolution contextual information, semantic accumulation, and adaptive computation. Beyond conventional dense prediction metrics, we use object-level evaluation to measure semantic understanding under sparse observations. On ADE20K-Object, a single foveated observation achieves 95.9% of the baseline Top-1 accuracy and 96.9% of the baseline Top-3 accuracy while requiring only 4.7% of the computational cost. At the scene level, semantic accumulation recovers 90.6% of the baseline object recall while using 58.6% of the computation. These results suggest that substantial semantic understanding can emerge from sparse observations when computation is allocated selectively, highlighting active vision as an efficient alternative to uniform dense processing and motivating evaluation protocols beyond conventional pixel-wise segmentation metrics.

title: Quantisation of Abstract Data Types
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a notion of abstract quantum data type within the framework of universal algebra. This notion provides an algebraic foundation for describing data abstraction in quantum programming. We formally define a quantisation of classical data types and show that their equational specifications can be soundly lifted to the quantum setting. Two standard quantisation methods for classical functions, namely the bit oracle and the phase oracle, arise as special cases of this general construction. We illustrate the framework with applications to quantum arrays and quantum error-correcting codes, showing how they can be understood through the lens of data-type quantisation. We further establish conditions under which quantisation preserves structural relationships and constructions of classical data types, including embeddings, isomorphisms, and products.

title: Rethinking World Models for Safety-Critical Embodied Systems
abstract: World models have progressed from compact latent dynamics to generative, controllable, and interactive simulators of embodied environments. However, high predictive likelihood and visual fidelity do not necessarily ensure that a model preserves the evidence required for safe decision-making. This perspective identifies three structural mismatches in current world modeling: likelihood versus risk, prediction versus intervention, and finite-horizon prediction versus accumulated consequences. We propose the Risk-Informed World Model (RIWM) as a decision-centric research direction for safety-critical embodied systems. RIWM organizes world modeling around consequences, intervention, epistemic uncertainty, and recoverability, and integrates four interdependent capabilities: decision-relevant representation, counterfactual reasoning, safety-critical episodic memory, and runtime safety assurance. It distinguishes physical, social, and operational consequences while using epistemic uncertainty to qualify the evidence supporting action. We further discuss open challenges in identifying consequential futures, validating counterfactual reasoning, maintaining revisable safety memories, translating learned consequences into executable constraints, and determining when evidence is sufficient to act. This perspective argues that future world models should move beyond predicting likely futures toward identifying which futures matter, revising judgments through experience, and recognizing when to act, revise, sense, defer, or abstain.

title: Quantum Probability Generation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum probability generation algorithms represent a paradigm shift in the design of probabilistic systems, moving beyond traditional methods reliant on fixed distributions. This paper investigates the theoretical and practical feasibility of a novel quantum algorithm, the Quantum Probability Generation Algorithm (QGPA), designed to produce sequences of probability distributions exhibiting desirable properties, including high information density and low error rate. The core mechanism leverages quantum superposition and entanglement to achieve this, offering a fundamentally different approach to generating complex probability distributions. The proposed algorithm demonstrates the potential for generating tailored distributions crucial for advanced data compression and error correction applications.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex system modeling leveraging the power of graph neural networks (GNNs). We construct a model designed to predict system behavior and states by effectively capturing relationships between nodes and edges within the system. The core mechanism of this approach is the utilization of GNNs to build a predictive architecture, offering a more efficient and insightful method compared to traditional approaches. The research demonstrates the efficacy of this model through comprehensive simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential for handling complex systems with intricate dynamics.

title: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Computing Architecture
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense potential, but current limitations stem largely from the difficulty of scaling quantum systems. This research proposes a novel quantum computation architecture centered around adaptive quantum entanglement. We introduce a "纠缠连接调整" (Entanglement Connection Adjustment) mechanism, allowing the system to dynamically adjust the connectivity between qubits in response to quantum state changes. This dynamic adjustment, guided by a self-optimizing algorithm, is designed to enhance computational efficiency and address the inherent scalability challenges of existing quantum architectures. This work explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations in current quantum computing paradigms and lay the groundwork for more efficient and versatile quantum computations.

title: 基于自适应的图论的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper explores the application of graph theory concepts to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of deep learning models. Traditional deep learning models often suffer from sensitivity to data variations and overfitting, limiting their performance on complex, high-dimensional datasets. We propose a novel machine learning algorithm, termed "Graph-Enhanced Deep Learning" (GEDL), that integrates graph-based regularization, node importance estimation, and structured learning techniques to mitigate these challenges. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph representation of the data and leveraging graph properties to guide model training and regularization. This approach aims to improve the model's ability to generalize to unseen data and reduce sensitivity to noise. We present a preliminary evaluation of GEDL on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its potential to enhance model performance.

title: 自适应神经网络的张量结构优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive neural network optimization algorithm based on tensor structure optimization. Traditional methods often rely on manual design, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. This algorithm leverages the inherent properties of tensors – specifically, their self-similarity and geometric properties – to automatically adjust network tensor structures, thereby enhancing both model expressiveness and generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves dynamically modifying the tensor's shape and connectivity to improve the network's ability to learn complex patterns. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over existing techniques, providing a robust and automated framework for optimizing neural network architectures. This research explores the potential of utilizing tensor structure as a key element in enhancing neural network performance.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Robotic Exploration with Hierarchical Predictive Control
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to robotic exploration by leveraging cognitive architectures. Existing robotic exploration systems often struggle with the dynamic and unpredictable nature of real-world environments, lacking the cognitive flexibility and adaptability observed in human exploration. This research addresses this limitation by developing a robotic exploration system grounded in a cognitive architecture that integrates hierarchical predictive control with a robust memory system. The core idea is to mimic human exploration strategies through a system capable of learning, planning, and adapting its behavior based on past experiences. The architecture utilizes a hierarchical structure to decompose exploration tasks into manageable sub-goals, coupled with predictive control to anticipate potential obstacles and opportunities. Furthermore, a memory system stores and retrieves past experiences, enabling the robot to generalize its knowledge and improve its exploration performance over time. The system's design emphasizes adaptability and learning, potentially leading to more efficient and robust exploration capabilities in complex and unknown environments. The primary contribution lies in the specific design of the cognitive architecture for robotic exploration, offering a pathway towards more human-like exploration behavior.

title: High-Order Quantum Adaptive Algorithm Parameter Optimization Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel high-order quantum adaptive algorithm parameter optimization framework. Traditional parameter optimization methods often rely on static adjustments, failing to fully leverage the dynamic behavior of quantum systems. Our framework dynamically adjusts quantum parameters based on real-time quantum computation results, offering a more effective optimization strategy. We propose a method that integrates optimization with quantum system dynamics, allowing for adaptive parameter tuning. This innovation aims to significantly enhance the performance of quantum algorithms by intelligently adjusting quantum parameters during the computation process. The proposed framework demonstrates improved results across a range of benchmark problems, showcasing its potential for advancing quantum computational capabilities.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding via Predictive Recurrence
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph embedding that explicitly incorporates temporal dynamics. Traditional graph embedding techniques typically treat graphs as static structures, neglecting the evolving relationships between nodes over time. We propose a method, Temporal Graph Embedding via Predictive Recurrence, which leverages recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to learn node embeddings that capture both the current structural information of the graph and the predictive influence of past interactions. The core idea is to iteratively update node embeddings within a temporal window, using observed connections and predicted future connections to drive the learning process. The integration of a GCN layer ensures that structural information remains a crucial component of the embedding, leading to more robust and informative representations. Our approach demonstrates the potential to significantly improve graph embedding quality by accounting for the dynamic nature of real-world graphs. We provide a detailed formulation of the method, including mathematical notations, and discuss its theoretical underpinnings. ---

title: Adaptive Multimodal Data Flow System (AMDFS)
abstract: This paper introduces the Adaptive Multimodal Data Flow System (AMDFS), a novel system designed for real-time analysis and processing of multimodal data streams. The core claim of AMDFS is to dynamically adjust data flow prioritization and processing methods based on data characteristics and user requirements. The system utilizes a hybrid signal processing approach for pre-processing and feature extraction across various modalities (text, image, audio, video), coupled with machine learning models for classification and priority ranking. This adaptive mechanism distinguishes AMDFS from traditional static multimodal systems, offering improved data utilization efficiency. The system's architecture and core mechanisms are detailed, outlining the key components and their interactions. The paper focuses on the dynamic adaptation strategy and its impact on overall system performance. The system's ability to learn and respond to evolving data patterns is presented as a key innovation. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and enhancements for AMDFS.

The system utilizes a hybrid signal processing approach for pre-processing and feature extraction across various modalities (text, image, audio, video), coupled with machine learning models for classification and priority ranking. This adaptive mechanism distinguishes AMDFS from traditional static multimodal systems, offering improved data utilization efficiency. The system's architecture and core mechanisms are detailed, outlining the key components and their interactions. The paper focuses on the dynamic adaptation strategy and its impact on overall system performance. The system's ability to learn and respond to evolving data patterns is presented as a key innovation. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and enhancements for AMDFS.

title: Distributed Theorem Proving with Evolutionary Strategies
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to distributed theorem proving (DTP) that leverages evolutionary strategies (ES) to address the limitations of traditional methods, particularly when dealing with large and complex theorems. The core idea is to employ ES to guide the exploration of the proof search space within a distributed environment. Each agent in the system evolves its proof strategy based on feedback from its success rate, resulting in a more efficient and robust proof process compared to purely random or rule-based approaches. We demonstrate the potential of this integrated framework to tackle previously intractable proof problems, offering a new paradigm for automated theorem proving. The key contribution lies in the dynamic adaptation of proof strategies through an evolutionary process, enhancing the system's ability to converge on valid proofs. The exploration of the proof space is significantly improved, leading to a higher probability of success in complex theorem verification.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Algorithmic Complexity
abstract: This paper explores the application of Bayesian constraint optimization to the challenge of optimizing algorithmic complexity. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, unpredictable algorithms, while existing approaches frequently rely on fixed, deterministic solutions. We propose a novel Bayesian framework that leverages probabilistic modeling to estimate the potential complexity of algorithms, enabling a more flexible and robust approach to design. The core mechanism involves constructing a probabilistic representation of the algorithm's state and potential for unexpected behavior, which is then used to guide the search for optimal solutions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through several illustrative examples focusing on machine learning and optimization, showcasing its ability to identify and refine complex algorithms. The paper's core claim is that a Bayesian approach offers a significant improvement over traditional methods in handling the inherent uncertainty and variability within algorithmic behavior.

abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network structure optimization method leveraging adaptive graph neural networks (GNNs). The core challenge in training GNNs lies in the dynamic adjustment of connection weights, which often requires extensive hyperparameter tuning. We introduce a new framework that dynamically adjusts the GNN's connectivity based on data-driven feature analysis. This adaptation mechanism, termed "Adaptive Weight Adjustment," significantly improves the network's expressiveness and generalization performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through experiments on several benchmark datasets, showcasing improvements in both accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed method offers a promising alternative to traditional static network architectures and offers a robust solution for optimizing GNNs.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Adaptive Topology Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum-enhanced adaptive topology discovery algorithm, termed "Quantum-Enhanced Adaptive Topology Discovery" (QAED). The algorithm leverages quantum mechanics to dynamically adjust parameters during the topological structure discovery process, enabling a more efficient and nuanced exploration of topological spaces. We propose a framework for quantifying and optimizing the search space, incorporating quantum-inspired optimization techniques to guide the algorithm's exploration. The core mechanism centers around a quantum-enhanced parameter adjustment process that iteratively refines the search based on a feedback loop, improving the ability to identify complex topological features. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and preliminary analysis, showcasing the potential for significantly accelerating and enhancing the discovery of topological structures compared to traditional methods. This work addresses a fundamental challenge in topology research by introducing a fundamentally new approach to parameter optimization.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing graph-based logical reasoning algorithms to validate quantum computation algorithms, offering a novel approach to quantum algorithm verification that surpasses traditional simulation-based methods. We propose a framework where the core mechanism involves constructing a graph representing the algorithm's state space and applying logical inference to this graph. The goal is to dynamically test the algorithm's behavior and identify potential errors through rigorous logical analysis. The paper details the design of a graph-based verification protocol, explores the benefits of this approach, and discusses preliminary results demonstrating improved efficiency and insight into quantum algorithm robustness. We conclude that this technique represents a significant advancement in quantum algorithm verification, offering a pathway to more reliable and efficient quantum computation.

title: 基于动态矩阵的自适应学习框架
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive learning framework based on dynamically adjusted matrices. Traditional machine learning algorithms often require manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and computationally expensive. This framework addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the weight matrix of the learning model, enabling automatic learning and parameter optimization, particularly effective in scenarios with sparse data. We introduce a dynamic matrix weighting scheme that adapts to the data distribution, mitigating the impact of data sparsity and improving model generalization. The framework's core mechanism centers around the ability to iteratively update the matrix weights based on the observed data, leading to enhanced performance compared to static weight initialization methods. This work explores the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic random matrix self-adaptation algorithm designed to dynamically adjust geometric transformations based on environmental changes. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of probability random matrices to learn and refine a transformation process, enabling data adaptation and representation. We propose a method that automatically identifies and modifies the matrix based on observed data, fostering a flexible and responsive system. This approach distinguishes it from existing techniques, which often rely on manually defined transformations or pre-determined mappings. This work demonstrates a practical implementation of this algorithm, showcasing its ability to effectively adapt to dynamic datasets. The algorithm's efficacy is validated through simulated and experimental scenarios, offering a robust foundation for future advancements in adaptive geometric representations.

abstract: Fractal dimension, traditionally defined as a measure of complexity, provides a novel and potentially powerful constraint for evolutionary algorithms. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of constraint-driven optimization and offers a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of evolutionary algorithms in complex, multi-dimensional spaces.

title: ##混沌动态网络优化算法 (CDNO)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, the混沌动态网络优化 (CDNO) algorithm, designed to address the challenges of complex dynamic network optimization, particularly in scenarios involving traffic flow and resource allocation. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with rapidly changing environments, necessitating more adaptable and efficient solutions. CDNO leverages dynamic chaos theory to achieve optimized solutions through a combination of adaptive control, dynamic network modeling, and iterative refinement. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a dynamic chaos model, allowing the algorithm to respond effectively to evolving network conditions. This paper details the algorithm's design, its key components, and its demonstrated performance on a variety of dynamic network optimization problems. We highlight the advantages of CDNO compared to existing methods, emphasizing its ability to handle complex, non-linear dynamics. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the application of this algorithm to further enhance optimization capabilities in dynamic network systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel reinforcement learning algorithm based on adaptive neural networks designed for optimizing complex control systems. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on manually defined reward functions, which can be difficult to design and may not capture the true desired behavior of the system. Our proposed algorithm leverages adaptive neural networks to automatically adjust control strategies, resulting in more effective control compared to traditional methods. We present a framework that allows the network to learn optimal control policies through self-adaptation, addressing the limitations of manual reward engineering. The core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted network structure that continuously learns and refines its parameters based on feedback, enabling more robust and adaptable control. The work explores the impact of network architecture and training techniques on the performance of the optimized control system.

title: Quantum Entanglement Simulation: A Quantum Information Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, offers a unique platform for simulating complex quantum systems. Traditional computational methods struggle to effectively handle these intricate systems, often requiring exponentially increasing computational resources. This paper introduces a novel quantum information adaptive algorithm based on the principles of quantum entanglement. The algorithm leverages the fragility of entanglement to dynamically adjust simulation parameters based on the outcome of the simulation, thereby enabling automated parameterization and optimization, significantly reducing computational cost. We present a detailed explanation of the core mechanism, including the mathematical formulation of the entanglement-based feedback loop and its impact on the simulation process. This research explores the potential of this approach to revolutionize quantum simulation, offering a pathway towards more efficient and adaptable simulations of complex quantum systems.

title: Dynamics of Metarepresentation and Structural Limits of Self Containment: A Diagonalization and Transfinite Cardinal Approach
abstract: We formalize the problem of epistemic self-containment in reflective agents usingstate-space representation and operator theory. By defining a metarepresentation operator Φover a family of cognitive frontiers F ⊆ P(U), we demonstrate that complete self-containmentis strictly impossible for any internal representation framework. Utilizing a Tarski-Cantor diag-onal argument, we prove that no finite internal frame can contain its own evaluation predicate,forcing a strictly ascending chain of representation frontiers F0 ⊊ F1 ⊊ F2 . . . . Furthermore, byanalyzing exhaustive metarepresentation through power-set dynamics, we map this expansionto the transfinite hierarchy of Beth numbers (ℶn). We conclude that the reflexive zero-pointlimit Fω is structurally inaccessible in finite steps, establishing a general barrier theorem forself-modeling systems with applications to recursive AI self-improvement, logical proof barriers,and physical observer bounds.

title: A Quantum Computing Method for AC Power Flow with Residual-Controlled Dynamic Precision
abstract: To address the amplification of correction errors caused by an ill-conditioned AC power-flow Jacobian under heavily loaded operating conditions, as well as the excessive circuit depth associated with a fixed quantum-solution accuracy, this paper proposes a residual-controlled, regularized quantum singular-value transformation (QSVT) method within an inexact Newton power-flow framework. First, the power-mismatch vector and state variables are scaled, and the Newton correction is reformulated as a Tikhonov-regularized least-squares subproblem. A bounded regularization filter is then approximated using Chebyshev polynomials, allowing QSVT to directly transform the singular values of the Jacobian matrix. On this basis, the residual of the linear subproblem associated with the quantum-approximate correction is defined, and constraints are established to relate the polynomial-approximation error, block-encoding error, and quantum measurement error to the inexact Newton forcing term. The QSVT polynomial degree and quantum-solution accuracy are subsequently adjusted dynamically according to the outer power-flow residual. Theoretical analysis establishes the boundedness of the regularized correction, a sufficient descent condition for the quantum-approximate correction, and the relationship between the solution error and cumulative query complexity under dynamically controlled quantum accuracy.

title: Topology-Aware Training and Spatial Diagnostics for Fiber Bundle Segmentation in Tracer Histology
abstract: Anatomic tracer studies reveal how axon bundles project from an injection site, branch into smaller groups of axons, and course through the brain to reach their destinations. Histological data from such studies provide anatomical reference information for validating diffusion MRI tractography. However, manual annotation of the histological data is very labor-intensive, and although automated segmentation methods have been proposed, they rely mainly on pixel-overlap losses such as BCE and Dice; topology-aware loss functions have not been studied for this task. We compare BCE-Dice, clDice, Betti matching, and Topograph for fiber bundle segmentation in macaque tracer histology using a frozen DINOv3 backbone. To our knowledge, this is the first exploration of foundation-model features for this task. BCE-Dice achieved the highest Dice, while clDice achieved the highest bundle recall but poor mask overlap. Topograph had similar Dice to BCE-Dice, the lowest $β_0$ error, and fewer false positives than BCE-Dice and Betti matching. Fiber bundle segmentation methods are typically evaluated with a permissive rule that counts a bundle as detected given any overlap with the prediction. We show this rule does not capture oversegmentation, and that per-section TPR can be inflated by empty sections assigned perfect recall. To quantify this, we introduce Excess32, a spatial diagnostic measuring predicted pixels outside a 32-pixel tolerance band around annotated bundles. In validation, a Betti-Topograph union raises sparse-bundle TPR from 0.818 to 0.933, but worsens FDR from 0.296 to 0.509, Excess32 from 0.108 to 0.466, and area ratio from 0.94 to 3.34. These results show detection metrics alone are insufficient to characterize segmentation quality.

title: A Non-Formulable Theorem: A Fundamental Limit of Finite Syntactic Systems and Its Consequences for Security and AI
abstract: For every coherent and sufficiently expressive finite syntactic system S, we prove the existence of at least one theorem that S cannot produce autonomously. The result is a metatheorem: it proves the existence of a theorem, and applies to every finite syntactic system - security mechanisms, AI systems, formal verifiers, legal systems, economic models, and the formal system in which it is itself proved.

title: Quantum Hamiltonian Evolution for Coherent Quantum Learning
abstract: We introduce Coherent Quantum Learning (CQL), a training framework for quantum learning models in which the model parameters are quantum degrees of freedom evolved under a Hamiltonian that encodes the loss function. Current quantum machine learning retains classical optimization: parameters are updated by a classical outer loop using gradient estimates from measurements, and quantum coherence has no role in the training dynamics, just as in any classical treatment of the same problem. In the quantum case, a parameter register initialized in superposition evolves unitarily, and probability amplitude concentrates near low-loss configurations through interference, without gradient computation or classical feedback. We give an explicit construction using block encodings and Hamiltonian simulation, applicable to arbitrary parameterized circuits. Numerical experiments on binary classification and interferometric phase estimation confirm that the evolved distribution peaks at the optimal parameters, matching gradient-based performance. The construction is compatible in principle with fault-tolerant implementations and extends to batched training via sequential Hamiltonian evolution.

title: An Adversarial Zero-Shot Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate IoT Traffic Data
abstract: Anomaly detection in Internet of Things (IoT) networks presents unique challenges due to the diversity of devices, lack of labeled data, and domain variability across environments. In this paper, we propose a novel framework for multivariate time-series anomaly detection that leverages adversarial learning and contrastive loss within a sequence-based Variational Autoencoder (VAE) architecture. Our method enables zero-shot domain adaptation by jointly optimizing domain-invariant latent representations and semantically structured embedding spaces, without requiring labeled data or raw feature transfer. To address the heterogeneity of IoT deployments, we introduce encoder and decoder adaptor layers that align feature distributions across domains while preserving contextual semantics. Additionally, we propose a destination-based segmentation strategy to better model real-world communication structures in IoT traffic. title: Override and Update in Restriction Categories

We provide various examples of override restriction categories and in particular show that every classical restriction category is an override restriction category.

title: Algorithmic Bias Mitigation via Differential Privacy (ABPD)
abstract: This paper introduces Algorithmic Bias Mitigation via Differential Privacy (ABPD), a novel approach to mitigating bias in machine learning models. Traditional bias mitigation techniques often involve post-processing or targeted data modifications, which can be computationally expensive and may not fully address the root cause of bias. ABPD leverages differential privacy, a rigorous privacy mechanism, to add controlled noise to the model parameters during training, effectively protecting against sensitive information while still allowing the model to learn effectively. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ABPD through a series of experiments on several benchmark datasets, showcasing a significant reduction in bias across multiple metrics. The core of the method involves a carefully crafted noise addition process that maintains model accuracy while minimizing the impact of sensitive data.

title: Dimension Reduction Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel dimension reduction theory based on the Gaussian process framework, designed to effectively reduce high-dimensional data while maximizing information retention. The core concept revolves around leveraging the power of Gaussian processes to achieve this goal, offering a robust and adaptable approach compared to traditional dimensionality reduction methods. The paper demonstrates the efficacy of this technique through a series of numerical experiments and analyzes its impact on various datasets, highlighting its potential for a wide range of applications.

abstract: Quantum computing is a rapidly advancing field with immense potential to revolutionize various industries. title: 基于图的量子态计算与优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational and optimization framework based on graph representations of quantum states. Traditional quantum algorithms often require direct manipulation of the quantum state, which can be computationally expensive and challenging. This work proposes a method that utilizes graph structures to simplify the optimization process inherent in quantum computations, leveraging the topological properties of the graphs to achieve efficiency gains. We present a new algorithm that transforms the optimization problem into a graph-based optimization, enabling a more streamlined and potentially faster approach to quantum state manipulation and optimization. The core mechanism centers around representing the quantum state as a graph, where nodes represent quantum states and edges define relationships and constraints. This graph representation allows for efficient exploration of the solution space and simplifies the optimization process by focusing on the structural properties of the graph rather than the individual quantum states. The potential advantages of this approach include reduced computational complexity, improved scalability, and a more intuitive understanding of the optimization process. We provide a theoretical analysis and initial implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in a specific quantum algorithm.

title: Neuroevolution of Adaptive Neurons
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design utilizing neuroevolution, specifically focusing on the adaptive design of individual neurons. The core concept involves employing an evolutionary algorithm to autonomously optimize the structural parameters of neurons, leading to the creation of highly specialized and energy-efficient neurons. Unlike traditional training methods that primarily adjust synaptic weights, this research directly manipulates neuron morphology – parameters such as synaptic connection weights, axon length, and dendrite size. The evolutionary process iteratively refines these parameters based on the neuron's performance within a defined task, utilizing a fitness function that quantifies this performance. The resulting adaptive neurons demonstrate a significant potential for improved efficiency and specialization compared to conventionally designed networks. The core algorithm is described in detail, highlighting the key components and their interactions. The method's capacity to create networks with bespoke neuron architectures tailored to specific tasks is explored. Finally, the potential for scaling this approach to larger and more complex neural networks is discussed.

title: ##基于量子纠错码的分布式存储系统设计
abstract: This paper proposes a design for a fault-tolerant distributed storage system leveraging quantum error-correcting codes. The core claim centers on using these codes to significantly enhance the reliability of data storage in a distributed environment. The proposed system employs quantum error-correcting codes for both encoding and decoding, effectively mitigating data corruption and ensuring data integrity. The novelty lies in the direct application of quantum error correction within a distributed storage architecture, addressing the inherent vulnerabilities of traditional storage systems to quantum decoherence and errors. This design offers a pathway towards robust data preservation in quantum computing scenarios. The system utilizes a layered approach, combining classical network infrastructure with quantum error correction protocols to achieve optimal performance. Key performance metrics such as error correction rate, storage overhead, and network latency are analyzed. The system's architecture is scalable and adaptable to varying storage requirements.

title: Dynamic Concept Graph Semantic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for dynamic concept graph semantic reasoning. The core idea is to construct a concept graph that can continuously update and evolve, and to leverage graph reasoning techniques for enhanced semantic understanding and knowledge discovery. The framework employs a dynamic graph structure based on knowledge graphs, integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to facilitate concept association learning and inference. Unlike static knowledge graphs, this approach addresses the inherent dynamism of knowledge by incorporating mechanisms for real-time adaptation and evolution. This results in a more accurate and timely understanding of complex semantic relationships. The system utilizes a series of algorithms to identify relevant concepts, establish connections, and perform reasoning based on the evolving graph structure. The key contribution lies in the combination of dynamic graph modeling with robust reasoning capabilities, enabling a more adaptive and intelligent semantic understanding system. The framework's performance is evaluated through simulated scenarios, demonstrating its ability to capture and reason about changing information effectively.

abstract: This paper explores the application of integrated geometry to formalize the principles of quantum information theory. We propose a novel model where quantum states are represented as points within a higher-dimensional space, and the evolution of these points is governed by complex differential equations. The core mechanism involves the development of a "Quantum Geometry" algorithm that automatically generates and analyzes quantum circuits based on geometric structures. This approach aims to move beyond a purely statistical view of quantum mechanics, establishing a geometric framework for understanding and manipulating quantum information.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Networks for Modeling Complex Social Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to modeling complex social systems utilizing Hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks often struggle to accurately represent the intricate, nested relationships and feedback loops inherent in social dynamics. This work argues that a hierarchical structure is essential for effectively capturing these complexities. The proposed framework allows for modeling social systems at multiple levels of abstraction, facilitating the analysis of social processes and prediction of behavior. The core mechanism involves constructing an HBN with interconnected Bayesian networks at different levels, where higher-level networks represent overarching social structures and lower-level networks detail specific interactions. The resulting model offers improved representational power and analytical capabilities compared to traditional Bayesian Network approaches. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology through a conceptual framework and outline key considerations for its implementation, highlighting the benefits of integrating multiple levels of analysis within a unified probabilistic framework. The model incorporates key elements such as agent interactions, social norms, and influence networks, allowing for a more nuanced understanding of social phenomena. Finally, we discuss the potential for future research and development in this area, including the application of HBNs to real-world social systems.

abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements, but inherent fragility necessitates robust error mitigation techniques. This approach offers a promising alternative to existing methods, potentially simplifying quantum computations while maintaining high accuracy.

title: Technologies quantiques pour l’énergie
abstract: Le document présente la stratégie d’EDF R&D autour des technologies quantiques appliquées à l’énergie. Face aux limites futures du calcul haute performance (HPC), notamment en complexité, coûts et consommation, le calcul quantique est envisagé à EDF R&D comme une perspective permettant d’aborder des problèmes aujourd’hui inaccessibles. Les cas d’usage couvrent toute la chaîne de valeur du système électrique : optimisation des réseaux et de la production, sûreté nucléaire via les études probabilistes, modélisation physique (équations aux dérivées partielles) et vieillissement des matériaux. L’entreprise s’appuie sur de nombreux partenariats industriels et académiques pour co-développer des algorithmes solutions. Des applications connexes, comme les capteurs quantiques pour la détection de défauts, sont également explorées. En conclusion, le quantique constitue un levier stratégique complémentaire pour anticiper les ruptures technologiques, et renforcer la performance du système électrique.
