title: Les technologies habilitantes : Organiser l’infrastructure de la seconde révolution quantique
abstract: La seconde révolution quantique est souvent appréhendée à travers les progrès des qubits et des algorithmes. Pourtant, le passage de démonstrateurs de laboratoire à des systèmes exploitables à grande échelle révèle un enjeu d’une autre nature : la capacité à organiser, intégrer et coordonner des technologies hétérogènes au sein de systèmes complexes. Cryogénie à très basse température, chaînes électroniques massives de contrôle et de lecture constituent une infrastructure immergée, mais déterminante, du quantique. Dans cet article, nous proposons une lecture organisationnelle et industrielle de ces technologies habilitantes, en montrant comment elles structurent les architectures des systèmes quantiques, les chaînes de valeur associées et les modes de coopération entre acteurs publics et privés. Nous mettons en évidence en quoi la transformation du calcul promise par la rupture scientifique de la seconde révolution quantique n’aboutira qu’en relevant de nombreux défis d’ingénierie.

title: A computational pathology-based AI framework for predicting PD-L1 expression and prognosis in HNSCC
abstract: Aim: To investigate interobserver variability in programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) combined positive score (CPS) assessment in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and to develop an artificial intelligence (AI)-based model for predicting PD-L1 expression and patient prognosis from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides. Methods: Fifty HNSCC specimens were independently evaluated for PD-L1 by pathologists with different experience levels. Agreement was assessed using Fleiss’ and Cohen’s κ. Whole-slide images were processed into tiles for deep learning using DenseNet121. Tile-level features were integrated via two machine learning pipelines to construct whole-slide prediction models. Multiple algorithms were tested, with performance evaluated in validation and testing cohorts. Prognostic value was analyzed using AI-derived risk stratification. Results: Interobserver agreement was low (Fleiss’ κ = 0.34), indicating substantial variability in CPS assessment. DenseNet121 achieved moderate predictive performance (AUC 0.641 in validation, 0.616 in testing). AI models significantly improved prediction accuracy, with logistic regression demonstrating the best performance (AUC 0.900 in validation, 0.851 in testing). AI-derived prediction scores effectively stratified overall survival, with multiple models showing significant prognostic discrimination (P < 0.05). Conclusions: AI models integrating deep learning and machine learning can accurately predict PD-L1 expression and stratify prognosis in HNSCC, outperforming tile-level deep learning alone.

title: Guiding the coarse levels of semantic IDs makes the fine levels learnable
abstract: Generative retrieval represents each item by a short Semantic ID and casts recommendation as autoregressive generation of that sequence. Because the tokenizer is trained independently to reconstruct an item embedding, its codes are aligned with neither the downstream LLM nor the end task. Nearly every SID system therefore spends extra effort to bridge this gap--alignment corpora, reasoning/RL, or per-token encoders to make codes legible, or learned tokenizer supervision to make them task-aware--yet the recovered meaning is content-derived and may not be the meaning the task needs. We introduce Guided SID, which instead makes the levels that matter most meaningful by construction: we force the coarse RQ-VAE levels to encode a predefined categorical attribute--chosen to be text-grounded (hence legible to the LLM) and task-relevant--by deterministic supervised index assignment (overriding nearest-neighbor selection with the attribute label) while keeping the codebooks learnable (they still receive reconstruction gradients). A trie-merge construction maps any high-cardinality or set-valued attribute onto the fixed code budget while keeping merged buckets semantically coherent. Guiding costs nothing intrinsically: collision and reconstruction match or beat the vanilla baseline despite pinning the coarse level. In a matched end-to-end A/B differing only in the SID encoding, the guided retriever improves recall@k at every list length we measure (1.36x at k=1, 1.39x at k=10), raises mean reciprocal rank from 0.0260 to 0.0355, and predicts the pre-defined attribute 4.2x more often.

title: Continuous Actions from Discrete Minds: Latent-Aligned Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
abstract: Bridging the gap between the discrete reasoning of Vision-Language Models and the continuous, physics-constrained nature of autonomous driving remains a significant challenge. In this work, we introduce LaPla, a unified Vision-Language-Action (VLA) framework featuring latent-aligned planning to seamlessly ground semantic understanding in precise motion execution. We first design an action tokenizer based on a residual vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE), capturing vehicle kinematics and encoding trajectory features into a structured latent space. Rather than discrete codebook lookups that inevitably introduce quantization errors, LaPla repurposes this representation as a physical prior to bridge the modality gap between high-dimensional semantics and the raw action space. Specifically, given multimodal inputs integrating multi-view images, historical actions, and textual instructions, LaPla incorporates concurrent action queries to causally attend to the multimodal context in a single forward pass, projecting hidden states directly into the pretrained VQ-VAE latent space. The frozen decoder then translates these continuous latents into actions, effectively eliminating quantization errors and ensuring physically plausible trajectories while bypassing time-consuming autoregressive generation. Extensive experiments on the nuScenes benchmark demonstrate that LaPla achieves competitive open-loop performance, reducing long-horizon L2 error by 15.52% compared to state-of-the-art VLA methods. Closed-loop evaluations on the NVIDIA AlpaSim simulator further confirm its superior capability in ensuring smooth driving progress, improving the success rate by 33.34 percentage points with significantly reduced inference latency.

title: Authorized but Not Preserving: A Boundary on Representation-Independent Identity in Gate-Mediated Systems
abstract: Agentic systems that bind real-world consequences through a gate also change the representations through which they operate: they migrate schemas, re-encode state, and rewrite the models by which every other transition is expressed. Whether anything is preserved across such a re-representation, and whether the mechanism that authorised it can tell, is not settled by the formalisms that address either authority or behavioural equivalence on their own. Behavioural equivalence presupposes a fixed observational vocabulary; information-theoretic sufficiency characterises what is recoverable rather than what may be committed; deontic accounts index authority to agents and acts rather than to change of representation. We ask whether a functional over representational states can be both representation-independent and gate-decidable. The direct route is circular — an admissible class defined by what it preserves guarantees the invariant it is then found to preserve — so admissibility is instead fixed by consequence-binding authority, and non-circularity is enforced by a contract that permits shared inputs but forbids the gate's verdict from tracking any candidate or decision-equivalent surrogate of one. The admissible class, observation map, block condition and domain assumption are sealed before a finite candidate space of seventeen functionals is declared and sealed in turn. Two results follow. Structurally, the two authority-indexed classes realise the properties disjointly: authority proper is representation-independent but not gate-decidable, while the gate's class decides membership by construction and is indexed by the representation on which it decides; the soundness axiom relates them in one direction only and the inclusion is strict. In execution, no candidate met the declared success conditions, and all fifteen substantive candidates — drawn from constitutive structure, consequence-class availability, threshold profiles and epistemic capacity — failed for one reason: the gate certifies epistemic adequacy for binding a transition's own consequence class and certifies nothing about what the transition preserves. The negative result is candidate-space exhaustion, not proved non-existence: no candidate in the sealed space realises the joint property under the frozen contract. The audit is formal, and its counterexamples turn on a stipulated witness rather than on deployment data. Authorisation and preservation are orthogonal within the frozen construction; a theory that recovers preservation must supply it from an independently specified source, declared before the candidate is evaluated.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Optimization for Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: Quantum annealing techniques are being explored as a potential advancement in optimization for constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing to accelerate the search for optimal solutions for CSPs, focusing on its ability to overcome the computational limitations of traditional methods, especially for large and complex problems. The core claim is that the introduction of quantum annealing can significantly enhance the efficiency of optimization, offering a pathway to more scalable solutions. This work will detail the theoretical framework, implementation details, and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach.

title: Title: Emergent Symmetry in Complex Systems via Bayesian Inference
abstract: Complex systems exhibit a remarkable degree of order despite their apparent randomness. This paper explores the potential of Bayesian inference as a novel approach to automatically discover and exploit emergent symmetry patterns within such systems. We propose a new algorithm that iteratively refines a probability distribution based on observed data, identifying patterns suggesting underlying symmetries. The goal is to predict the long-term stability of these systems, moving beyond traditional methods that rely on explicit symmetry definitions. This work utilizes Bayesian methods to continuously update the probability distribution, offering a more flexible and potentially powerful tool for analyzing complex systems. This approach aims to uncover hidden symmetries and predict stability, a challenge currently addressed with limited success. The paper details the algorithm's architecture, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses the implications for understanding and modeling complex phenomena.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-linear topological geometry as a foundation for novel quantum algorithms. We propose a new quantum algorithm, leveraging the inherent structure and topological properties of these spaces, to achieve enhanced efficiency and performance compared to existing quantum approaches. The core mechanism centers around manipulating quantum states through geometric transformations, specifically designed to exploit the unique characteristics of non-linear topology. This research explores the fundamental implications of this approach and highlights the potential for significant advancements in quantum computation.

title: Dynamic Quantum State Generation & Topology Structure Correlation
abstract: This paper investigates the generation of dynamic quantum states utilizing topological structures to create complex topological structures and dynamic variations in quantum states. The core focus is on a novel dynamic quantum state generation method that integrates topological principles to achieve quantum states with intricate topologies and dynamic behavior, offering enhanced capabilities for advanced quantum computation. We present a framework that leverages the inherent properties of topological phases to generate quantum states with unprecedented flexibility. The resulting quantum states exhibit characteristics not readily achievable through conventional methods, underscoring the significance of this approach.

title: 基于图的自适应机器学习的动态网络结构优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic network structure optimization in machine learning, leveraging graph-based machine learning models. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static network configurations, limiting their adaptability to evolving data and task demands. Our method proposes a system that dynamically adjusts the graph's structure—specifically, node and edge manipulation—based on network state changes. This adaptive approach enhances network efficiency and performance, offering a significant improvement over static network configurations. The core mechanism involves implementing a self-adjusting graph structure optimization algorithm, which utilizes graph theory principles to dynamically modify network topology. We present a comprehensive implementation of this algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness across a range of machine learning tasks, showcasing its ability to improve model accuracy and speed.

title: Relational Quantum Circuit Compilation via Tensor Networks
abstract: Quantum circuit compilation is a critical step in realizing quantum computation, aiming to translate high-level quantum algorithms into a sequence of low-level gate operations executable on a quantum hardware. Traditional compilation methods often suffer from exponential scaling in the representation of the quantum state space, leading to prohibitive computational costs. This work introduces a novel approach to quantum circuit compilation utilizing tensor networks. We represent quantum circuits and their resulting states as higher-order tensor networks, enabling efficient manipulation and contraction of these representations. Our algorithm leverages tensor contraction and permutation techniques specifically tailored to the inherent structure of quantum circuits, minimizing the rank of the tensor networks and, consequently, reducing computational overhead. This approach offers the potential for significant speedups compared to conventional compilation techniques, addressing the core challenge of exponential scaling in quantum state representation. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through theoretical analysis and a novel compilation algorithm.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Theoretical Framework for Noise Generalization
abstract: This paper presents a novel theoretical framework for understanding noise generalization in quantum machine learning (QML). We address the critical gap in current research, which predominantly relies on experimental validation, by developing a mathematically rigorous approach. Our core claim centers on establishing a quantifiable relationship between noise levels and the generalization performance of QML models. We leverage quantum decoherence theory and quantum error correction concepts to analyze the impact of noise on model parameters. Utilizing tools from functional analysis and norm theory, we derive a theoretical model for noise generalization. Furthermore, we propose strategies for mitigating the detrimental effects of noise, offering potential avenues for enhancing the robustness of QML systems. This work provides a foundational understanding for future QML design and optimization, moving beyond empirical observations toward a predictive and controllable approach.

title: Algorithmic Constraint Optimization for Fractal Dimension Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces an algorithmic constraint optimization framework for the discovery of fractal dimension in complex datasets. The core focus is on leveraging evolutionary computation to automatically identify and quantify fractal patterns within data. We propose a novel approach that integrates reinforcement learning with a genetic algorithm to dynamically refine fractal shape representations, thereby enabling the algorithm to uncover previously unseen fractal characteristics. The algorithm's design prioritizes robustness and adaptability, addressing limitations of current methods that rely heavily on manual design. This work represents a significant step towards automated fractal dimension estimation and pattern recognition, offering a flexible and potentially transformative tool for various scientific and engineering disciplines.

title: Explainable AI for Cybersecurity Threat Detection via Causal Reasoning
abstract: The increasing sophistication of cyber threats demands more effective and reliable detection systems. However, many current Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based cybersecurity solutions operate as "black boxes," lacking transparency and hindering trust. This research addresses this critical gap by integrating Explainable AI (XAI) techniques with causal reasoning to create a more understandable and actionable cybersecurity threat detection system. We construct a causal Bayesian network that explicitly models the relationships between network events and potential threats. Subsequently, XAI methods are applied to interpret the reasoning process of the system, highlighting the key causal pathways leading to threat detections. This approach offers a novel way to explain the complex decision-making processes of AI systems in cybersecurity, fostering greater trust, facilitating targeted investigations, and ultimately improving threat response capabilities. The core contribution lies in the synergistic combination of causal inference and XAI, moving beyond simply explaining correlations to providing genuine causal understanding.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Computation on Analog Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of computation achievable by analog neural networks (ANNs) through an information-theoretic lens. We establish rigorous bounds on the computational capacity of ANNs by analyzing the information flow and processing capabilities within these networks. This analysis utilizes concepts such as entropy, mutual information, and channel capacity to quantify the information transformation performed by ANNs during computation. The core contribution lies in providing a precise framework for understanding the inherent constraints imposed by the analog nature of ANNs, differentiating them from their digital counterparts. Specifically, we derive expressions relating the network architecture (connectivity, synaptic weights) to the achievable information processing rate and the associated entropy. Furthermore, we explore the impact of noise and uncertainty on information transmission within ANNs, highlighting the role of robust coding schemes in maximizing computational performance. The results demonstrate that the computational power of ANNs is fundamentally limited by the information-theoretic properties of the underlying physical channels, regardless of the network's complexity. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for the design and optimization of ANNs for specific computational tasks.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Explainable AI – Bayesian Inference Chains with Causal Reasoning
abstract: The growing deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, particularly in critical domains like healthcare and finance, necessitates transparency and interpretability – concepts often lacking in "black box" models. This paper proposes a novel approach to explainable AI (XAI) by integrating Bayesian inference chains with causal reasoning within a cognitive architecture framework. The core idea is to move beyond simply identifying influential features to constructing a transparent, step-by-step explanation of *why* an AI system reached a particular decision. We introduce a system that leverages probabilistic inference within Bayesian networks, augmented with causal relationships, to trace the reasoning pathways leading to a prediction. This approach allows for a more robust and trustworthy explanation by explicitly modeling the underlying causal drivers. The generated explanations are presented as a chain of inferences, detailing the influence of various factors at each stage, providing a level of understanding unattainable with traditional feature attribution methods. The paper outlines the key components of this architecture and discusses its potential benefits and future research directions.

title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Network Self-Adaptive Polynomial Fitting
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for adaptive polynomial fitting, leveraging a self-organizing network to dynamically adjust polynomial coefficients based on the system's internal dynamics. The core concept is to create a network architecture that, upon input, continuously evaluates the system's state and adjusts the polynomial coefficients to minimize prediction errors. We propose a dynamic weighting scheme to determine the importance of different polynomial terms, ensuring that the model captures the relevant patterns within the data without unnecessary complexity. The framework aims to significantly improve the predictive accuracy of polynomial models compared to static approaches, particularly in scenarios where the system's dynamics are complex and non-stationary. This work presents a rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrates its effectiveness through a series of simulations and experiments.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Lattice Theory for Complex Systems
abstract: Quantum-enhanced lattice theory offers a novel approach to modeling complex systems, particularly those exhibiting strong correlations and dynamic behavior. This paper explores the potential of extending lattice theory to incorporate quantum mechanics principles, specifically focusing on the dynamics of highly correlated systems. We introduce a quantum algorithm designed to efficiently calculate entanglement and correlations within a lattice, aiming to significantly enhance simulation accuracy compared to classical methods. This research addresses the limitations of traditional lattice methods in capturing intricate patterns and predicting complex system evolution, providing a pathway towards more precise modeling and control. The core mechanism involves the integration of quantum mechanics into lattice dynamics, offering a promising shift towards a fundamentally different approach to complex system analysis.

title: Topological Quantum Computing: A Novel Approach to Heterogeneous Qubit Connectivity
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to achieving high-fidelity and scalable quantum computation through heterogeneous qubit connectivity within a topological quantum computing framework. The core challenge in topological quantum computing lies in effectively connecting qubits of diverse types – differing in their physical realization and control mechanisms – to enable complex quantum algorithms. This work proposes a system leveraging topological networks to establish these connections, capitalizing on quantum entanglement to facilitate information transfer and control across disparate qubit architectures. The proposed method addresses a critical bottleneck in the development of topological quantum computers by offering a fundamentally new strategy for heterogeneous qubit integration. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key principles and potential advantages of this approach, emphasizing the realization of robust, scalable, and versatile quantum systems. We detail the conceptual design, focusing on entanglement distribution and error mitigation strategies specific to this architecture. The ultimate goal is to demonstrate a pathway towards building quantum computers capable of tackling complex problems requiring diverse qubit capabilities.

title: Title: Quantum-Entangled Variable Drift (QEDD)
abstract: Quantum-Entangled Variable Drift (QEDD) presents a novel framework for quantifying and mitigating the effects of quantum entanglement on system behavior, particularly focusing on the 'drift' of variables across entangled pairs. Existing approaches often struggle with the complexities of entanglement, leading to unpredictable system behavior. This paper introduces a probabilistic model, the QEDD framework, that explicitly incorporates uncertainty inherent in entanglement, allowing for a more robust and predictive analysis of variable evolution. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulations, revealing a significant reduction in observed drift compared to traditional approaches. This work addresses a fundamental challenge in quantum systems – the inherent instability of entanglement – offering a pathway towards more stable and controllable quantum systems.

title: Constraint Preservation and Multi-Stage Refinement: An Agent Optimization Framework for Literary Writing
abstract: The bottleneck of Large Language Models in creative writing lies not in generation, but in goal-directed optimization — improving literary quality while adhering to formal constraints. We propose the first agent optimization framework to explicitly separate hard constraints (formally verifiable, e.g., tonal patterns) from soft constraints (requiring aesthetic judgment, e.g., refined diction) in literary writing. Grounded in two complete case studies — classical Chinese regulated verse prosody correction and prose imagery closure generation — the framework contributes: (1) a formalization of mixed-constraint writing optimization; (2) a dual-axis architecture mandating hard-constraint-first ordering; (3) an invariant preservation principle protecting authorial intent; (4) a divergent-convergent search pattern for soft-constraint problems; and (5) a three-tier knowledge architecture. Case A achieved full prosody correction at a 6.7% modification rate; Case B produced four orthogonally varying closure candidates with a three-dimension evaluation rubric. We discuss applicability boundaries, limitations, and generalization pathways.

title: Probability Logic for Dynamic Adaptable Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic logic framework designed to optimize complex algorithms through dynamic adaptation. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting their ability to handle varying environments and complex problem structures. This work proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on probabilistic logic, enabling the algorithm to intelligently adjust its parameters in response to changing input conditions and desired outcomes. The framework leverages the inherent strengths of probabilistic reasoning to achieve superior performance and robustness compared to conventional optimization methods. We explore the design of this framework, demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of illustrative examples and analysis. The paper details the core mechanism, including the probabilistic logic model and its integration with an optimization algorithm. It concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this approach.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity Modeling for Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive complexity modeling to machine learning algorithms, aiming to enhance both performance and generalization capabilities. The core challenge lies in dynamically adjusting the model's complexity – the number of parameters or layers – as the data undergoes processing, reflecting the inherent variability of the input. We propose a novel method that establishes a self-tuning complexity parameter, which adjusts based on data distribution, enabling the model to adapt to the data's characteristics and optimize for improved accuracy and robustness. The research explores the benefits of this dynamic approach compared to static complexity settings, demonstrating improvements across a range of benchmark datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for future machine learning development.

title: Quantum-Accelerated Evolutionary Algorithms for Parameter Space Optimization
abstract: Quantum-accelerated evolutionary algorithms (QEA) represent a novel approach to optimization, utilizing quantum mechanics to enhance exploration and convergence speed. This paper explores the potential of QEA to address challenges inherent in traditional evolutionary algorithms, particularly in parameter space optimization. We detail the implementation of quantum annealing and quantum-inspired optimization as core mechanisms, demonstrating their efficacy in accelerating the search process. The core claim posits that QEA's quantum properties will yield superior performance compared to classical algorithms. This research investigates the feasibility of leveraging quantum phenomena to improve the efficiency of evolutionary optimization, ultimately offering a pathway toward more robust and rapid solution discovery.

title: Adaptive Geometry Transformation Quantum Computing Implementation (AGTQC)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum computing, focusing on the implementation of adaptive geometry transformations. The core claim is that a novel algorithm, AGTQC, can efficiently and accurately perform complex geometric transformations using quantum entanglement and self-adaptive transformations, thereby enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms. We detail the design of AGTQC, exploring its underlying principles and potential applications. This work addresses a significant challenge in quantum computing – the limitations of classical algorithms in handling intricate geometric operations – and proposes a pathway towards more powerful and versatile quantum computations.

title: MetriQs-France : Levier stratégique pour la compétitivité des entreprises des technologies quantiques
abstract: S’inscrivant dans la Stratégie nationale sur les technologies quantiques, MetriQs-France est le programme consacré aux référentiels de mesure, à l’évaluation et à la normalisation des technologies quantiques. Coordonné par le LNE, il soutient l’émergence d’une industrie quantique durable réalisant les promesses du domaine, dans le contexte d’une vive compétition internationale. Le programme vise la mise en place d’un système d’assurance qualité complet, fondé sur une métrologie forte, en soutien à l’innovation et à la compétitivité des entreprises. Avec une subvention publique de 13 M€ (2022-2028), MetriQs-France s’articule suivant deux axes complémentaires, autour de la fourniture de spécifications techniques fiables : i) le développement et l’exploitation de méthodes de mesure de référence (projets de R&D collaboratifs, coopérations internationales et normalisation) ; et ii) le déploiement d’une infrastructure experte et indépendante, ouverte aux utilisateurs académiques et industriels les mettant en œuvre. Ainsi, le programme entend contribuer à lever les verrous technologiques, mettre en place une filière industrielle solide et souveraine, des chaînes d’approvisionnement sûres, et démontrer l’avantage des technologies quantiques par rapport aux technologies existantes pour en accélérer l’adoption par le marché.

title: Psy2Vec: Zero Fine-tuning Persona Vector Learning with Differentiable Soft-Label Gradient Descent and User-Defined Psychometric Scales
abstract: Role Persona Injection is critical for improving role consistency in large language models. However, existing vector-based steering methods—such as Persona Vectors and Linear Personality—rely on statistical mean differences or linear regression, which operate at a coarse semantic granularity and struggle to precisely calibrate "multiple-choice distributional responses"; moreover, the optimal steering layer is often selected heuristically. To address these issues, we propose Psy2Vec, Zero Fine-tuning Persona Vector Learning with Differentiable Soft-Label Gradient Descent and User-Defined Psychometric Scales. First, we adopt a configurable "category–dimension–item" structured scale, which allows dimensions and items to be freely added or removed. Then, we employ a Tutor Model to output option percentages, forming soft-labels carried by the character's option probability distribution. Next, through Computed Optimal Steering Layer Selection, we compare the activation gaps between high- and low-persona conditions layer by layer to derive the optimal steering layer, thereby replacing heuristic selection. Finally, we optimize the persona vector via differentiable RMSE gradient descent, achieving zero fine-tuning throughout without modifying any model weights. Preliminary experiments comparing both approaches on the same questionnaire demonstrate that Psy2Vec achieves lower persona-consistency error.

title: ATLAS: An Agent-based Training and Learning Analytics System for Rapid Deployment of Virtual Agent Studies
abstract: Running studies with virtual agents is a multi-faceted process. Apart from building and configuring an agent, it also requires proper infrastructure to host the agent, enrollment infrastructure for participants, learner tracking, pre/post session activities, and analytics. Existing platforms address different parts of this problem, but there is a lack of a comprehensive solution. We present ATLAS (Adaptive Training and Learner Analytics System), a web-based platform that integrates a drag-and-drop course authoring tool, a 3D virtual agent runtime with text-to-speech capabilities, and educator analytics in a single deployable system.

title: Towards AI-Driven Nanomedicine Discovery: A Benchmark and Multimodal Learning Framework for Nano Self-Assembly Prediction
abstract: Nano self-assembly organizes molecular components into bioactive nanoscale structures. Self-assembled nanoparticles (NAPs) derived from Chinese herbal formulas and applications such as anti-lung-cancer therapy demonstrate the substantial potential of self-assembly for nanomedicine discovery. Yet discovery still relies on costly wet-lab screening, while existing machine learning approaches lack standardized tasks, effective pairwise compatibility modeling, and public benchmarks with unified evaluation. To address these limitations, we formalize NSA prediction as a binary classification task for predicting self-assembly between molecular pairs and then establish NSA-Bench, the first public benchmark with curated molecular combinations, experimental conditions, self-assembly labels, and standardized evaluation protocols. We further develop NSA-Net, an interaction-aware multimodal framework that integrates complementary molecular evidence from graph topology, sequence semantics, and physicochemical descriptors to learn molecular-pair representations for self-assembly prediction. Extensive experiments on NSA-Bench show that NSA-Net achieves a ROC-AUC of $0.9470\pm0.0112$ (Small) and $0.9492\pm0.0062$ (Large). On the Small track, it surpasses the strongest machine-learning and graph-based baselines by 3.9 and 17.1 percentage points, respectively. Representation analyses reveal interpretable molecular characteristics associated with self-assembly prediction captured by the learned representations. Moreover, an NSA-Agent case study further demonstrates how NSA-Net predictions can support formulation refinement through experimental-condition-aware reasoning. Our code is available at https://github.com/developer-hq/NSA-Net.

title: Auditing Contextual Bias in Human Ball-Strike Calls Using KBO's Automated Umpiring Transition
abstract: This paper uses the Korean Baseball Organization's adoption of the Automated Ball-Strike (ABS) system to audit long-standing claims about contextual bias in human ball-strike calls. Using pitch-level KBO data from 2021 through the available portion of the 2026 season, we model called-strike probability for taken pitches near the strike-zone boundary, with 2022-2023 as the primary human-umpire baseline and ABS seasons (2024 and onward) as a diagnostic benchmark. The strongest evidence concerns count pressure. Relative to 0--0 counts, human umpires called substantially fewer strikes in two-strike counts and more strikes in hitter-ahead three-ball counts. Specifically, in the main 0.25-ft boundary band, 0--2 was associated with a -17.17 percentage-point effect and 3--0 with a +6.61 percentage-point effect. Under ABS, the corresponding effects were close to zero and did not survive false-discovery-rate correction. Game progression shows a smaller but coherent pattern as human calls were less strike-prone in early innings and more strike-prone in innings 7--9+, especially in late-close situations, while complete ABS seasons were essentially flat. Other suspected biases are weaker or more localized. Salary-based reputation proxies provide suggestive but proxy-sensitive evidence, and catcher identity shows human-period residual heterogeneity that disappears under ABS. Home-context evidence is mostly null at the umpire level, with one FDR-significant human-period exception and an exploratory umpire-team gap best treated as an audit lead. Overall, the results do not show that human umpires were biased everywhere. Instead, they map where the human strike zone was most context-sensitive, where evidence was weaker, and where common suspicions received little support.

title: Supplementary material from "Adding capabilities to AI-agent populations can worsen collective outcomes"
abstract: When resources are scarce, will the AI agents in our phones, medical devices, cars or drones coordinate smoothly, or interfere with one another? We study populations built from large language models competing for a capacity-limited resource. We compare increasing combinations of model diversity, simple reward-driven adaptation and programmed social sensing and grouping. When capacity is scarce, the populations with more capabilities overload far more often than a capacity-matched independent reference. Some agents also earn high rewards while the population fails. No capability is always helpful or harmful: its effect depends on capacity and on the other capabilities that are present. Our findings suggest that the capacity-to-population ratio can be an important guide in the design of systems that involve AI agents competing for some limited resource.

title: SBKIM: A Protocol for Semantic Bidirectional AI Matching in Human and Agent Networks
abstract: We propose SBKIM (Semantic Bidirectional AI Matching), an open protocol fordetermining semantic compatibility between two parties in natural language,without structured queries, databases or centralised platforms. Unlikeunidirectional retrieval systems, SBKIM requires that both parties describetheir capabilities and their needs at the same time. A language model ratesthe pair on three orthogonal dimensions and returns a structuredcompatibility report. The protocol operates on two layers: layer 1 forhuman-to-human matching (buyer/supplier, employee/project) and layer 2 foragent-to-agent matching in multi-agent systems. This is a field report, not a novelty claim: the building blocks are known,the operation is the contribution. A working reference implementation ispublicly available, and the traffic of the running network can be observedthrough a read-only network map. The German version of this paper is included as a second file. Reference implementation: https://github.com/lausiklauskn-png/Sage-Protokol

title: Adaptive Probability Distribution Geometry Evaluation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric complexity evaluation method based on adaptive probability distribution models. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of a probability distribution function to optimize the model's expressiveness and generalization ability. We propose a self-adjusting probability measure function that leverages the characteristics of the input data to automatically refine the distribution's parameters. This approach offers a more flexible and automated method for assessing model complexity compared to traditional methods relying on manual parameter tuning. The proposed method demonstrates improved performance in various benchmark datasets, highlighting the benefits of adaptive probability distribution modeling.

title: Quantum-Inspired Symbolic Regression for System Identification
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical models from data. However, traditional SR methods often suffer from limitations in exploring the vast search space for complex, non-linear system models, leading to computational bottlenecks and suboptimal solutions. This paper proposes a novel approach, Quantum-Inspired Symbolic Regression (QISR), that leverages quantum-inspired algorithms, specifically, analogs of quantum annealing, to address these challenges. QISR utilizes concepts like superposition and interference to concurrently evaluate a multitude of potential model expressions, drastically accelerating the discovery process. The core of the method lies in a cost function that balances model complexity with the quality of the fit to the observed data. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, that this approach has the potential for exponential speedup compared to conventional SR techniques, particularly when dealing with highly complex system dynamics. The key innovation is the adaptation of quantum heuristics to the classical problem of model discovery, offering a promising avenue for automating and accelerating the identification of accurate and insightful system models.

title: Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Complex Network Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex network control utilizing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). The core claim is that MARL offers a viable framework for optimizing and coordinating complex networks. The proposed mechanism involves treating each node within the network as an individual agent, equipped with a reinforcement learning algorithm to autonomously learn and execute control strategies. This research addresses the challenges of decentralized control in complex systems, aiming to enhance network efficiency and stability. The presented methodology demonstrates the potential for MARL to adapt to dynamic network conditions and achieve superior performance compared to traditional centralized control methods. The focus is on the theoretical underpinnings and design principles of this approach, outlining a framework for future research and implementation. ---

evidence.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex network control utilizing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). The core claim is that MARL offers a viable framework for optimizing and coordinating complex networks. The proposed mechanism involves treating each node within the network as an individual agent, equipped with a reinforcement learning algorithm to autonomously learn and execute control strategies. This research addresses the challenges of decentralized control in complex systems, aiming to enhance network efficiency and stability. The presented methodology demonstrates the potential for MARL to adapt to dynamic network conditions and achieve superior performance compared to traditional centralized control methods. The focus is on the theoretical underpinnings and design principles of this approach, outlining a framework for future research and implementation. ---

title: Distributed Symbolic Regression with Semantic Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its computational complexity, particularly with high-dimensional datasets and complex relationships, often hinders its effectiveness. Furthermore, standard SR algorithms frequently lack a semantic understanding of the underlying problem, leading to the generation of irrelevant or nonsensical equations. This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed symbolic regression that addresses these limitations. We introduce a system where multiple nodes collaboratively perform SR on subsets of the data, guided by a central node responsible for enforcing semantic constraints. These constraints, derived from domain expertise or data statistics, ensure that the generated equations are not only mathematically valid but also semantically meaningful. The system leverages distributed computing to accelerate the regression process and the constraint propagation mechanism to reduce the search space, ultimately leading to more accurate and interpretable models. The core claim is that incorporating semantic understanding into SR significantly improves its efficiency and quality. The key mechanism involves a distributed network of regression engines coupled with a centralized constraint management unit. This approach aims to overcome the traditional bottlenecks of SR, paving the way for its application in a wider range of complex scientific and engineering problems.

title: Symbolic Regression with Evolutionary Algorithms and Neural Symbolic Integration
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to symbolic regression, aiming to automatically discover mathematical equations from data. The core idea is to synergistically combine the strengths of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) and neural networks. EAs are utilized to generate candidate equations, while a neural network learns symbolic representations of the data. This integration facilitates improved accuracy and efficiency in the equation discovery process. We detail the architecture, training methodology, and integration strategy. The proposed method demonstrates promising results in uncovering complex mathematical relationships from diverse datasets, addressing a significant challenge in data science and scientific discovery. The primary equation discovery mechanism is described as: `E(x) = f(x)` where `E` represents the equation, `x` represents the independent variables, and `f` represents the unknown function. The evolutionary algorithm's fitness function is defined as: `Fitness(E) = 1 - |E(x_i) - y_i|` for `i = 1, 2, ..., N`, where `x_i` represents the input data point and `y_i` represents the corresponding output data point. The neural network's output is a symbolic representation, denoted as `S`, which is then used to guide the equation generation process. The loss function for the neural network is: `Loss = Σ ||S - SymbolicRepresentation(E(x_i))||²` for `i = 1, 2, ..., N`.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Error Propagation
abstract: Neural networks, despite their remarkable success in various domains, are susceptible to error accumulation during the training process. This accumulation often leads to instability and reduced accuracy, particularly in complex architectures and datasets. This paper proposes a novel architecture for neural networks – the Self-Correcting Neural Network (SCNN) – designed to mitigate this issue. The SCNN employs a sophisticated error propagation mechanism that actively monitors and corrects errors in both the network's activations and gradients. The core idea is to introduce feedback loops that allow the network to identify and reduce the impact of erroneous calculations, thereby promoting more stable and accurate learning. We present a detailed formulation of the SCNN, including the error propagation equations and the architectural considerations. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential for improved convergence and accuracy compared to traditional training methods. We outline the key components of the SCNN, including the error estimation module, the correction module, and the integration of these into the standard backpropagation algorithm. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions, focusing on adaptive error thresholds and more sophisticated correction strategies.

title: Probability Neural Network Dynamic Entropy Adjustment Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic neural network (PNN) dynamic entropy adjustment algorithm. Traditional neural network training methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting model performance. We propose a new approach that utilizes entropy as a learning objective, dynamically adjusting network parameters to improve generalization and prediction accuracy. The core mechanism involves iteratively assessing prediction errors and adjusting parameters based on these errors, guided by a dynamically updated entropy function. This adaptive approach offers a significant advancement in PNN training, potentially yielding superior model performance compared to existing methods. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of experiments evaluating its performance on various benchmark datasets.

title: Quantum Entanglement Entropy Information Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to information theory, leveraging quantum entanglement entropy as a fundamental measure of information. We propose that entanglement entropy can effectively quantify the efficiency of information transmission and provides a theoretical foundation that surpasses the limitations of classical information theory. The core of this work lies in the integration of entanglement entropy with Shannon entropy, establishing a new framework for analyzing information transfer. We explore scenarios where classical information theory struggles to adequately describe the limits of communication due to quantum mechanical effects, specifically entanglement. The paper aims to provide a theoretical underpinning for quantum communication protocols and potentially inform the development of quantum computation. We define key terms and formulate core concepts, focusing on the relationship between entanglement entropy, information content, and the constraints imposed by quantum mechanics. The central argument is that by considering the inherent interconnectedness of entangled systems, we can gain a deeper understanding of information processing at the most fundamental level. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Enhancement via Adaptive Correction
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers unprecedented computational capabilities. However, harnessing entanglement for practical applications remains a significant challenge due to its inherent fragility and susceptibility to decoherence. This paper explores a novel approach to quantum entanglement enhancement utilizing an adaptive correction scheme. We present a fundamentally different algorithm that dynamically adjusts the strength of entangled states, mitigating decoherence and enabling more precise quantum computations. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors and corrects the entanglement, optimizing the system's performance. This approach contrasts with traditional, static entanglement manipulation techniques, offering a pathway towards more efficient and reliable quantum computation.

title: 基于自适应的数学自动化的语言
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to mathematical theorem proving, leveraging an adaptive language model to automate the generation of proof processes. Traditional theorem proving methods rely heavily on manual design and are often susceptible to human error. Our proposed system aims to drastically simplify this process by utilizing an automated generation mechanism, reducing the need for extensive manual intervention. We present a framework that dynamically adjusts parameters to produce a diverse range of proof strategies. The core mechanism focuses on iterative refinement of proof steps based on predefined constraints and generated candidate proofs. This eliminates the need for iterative manual trial and error, leading to increased efficiency and reduced risk of errors. The benefits of this approach are demonstrated through a series of examples involving complex mathematical proofs. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future directions and limitations of the system.

title: Topological Data Compression with Adaptive Representation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel data compression technique, Topological Data Compression (TDC), designed to efficiently compress data by exploiting topological properties. Traditional compression methods struggle with data redundancy, while TDC focuses on maintaining essential relationships, leading to a more robust and adaptable compression algorithm. The core mechanism leverages graph representation and topological features to identify and compress redundant information, ultimately resulting in a significantly reduced data footprint. This approach offers a promising path toward more efficient data storage and transmission, particularly in scenarios where preserving data integrity is paramount.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of algorithmic quantum simulation to accelerate the study and analysis of complex, multi-dimensional dynamical systems. We introduce a novel quantum algorithm designed to efficiently explore the state space of these systems, offering a significant advantage over classical simulation techniques, particularly for systems with intricate dynamics and high dimensionality. We outline the algorithm's architecture, key quantum operations, and potential applications within diverse fields such as physics, chemistry, and materials science. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the expected impact of this approach on the field of quantum computation.

title: Title: Probabilistic Bayesian Modeling of Emergent Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic Bayesian modeling framework designed to address the challenges of understanding and predicting complex, interacting systems. The core claim is to create a system capable of simultaneously modeling multiple, interacting systems, where the emergent behavior is governed by a probabilistic Bayesian process. We propose a novel Bayesian inference algorithm optimized for handling complex dependencies and non-linear interactions, facilitating the prediction of system states and dynamics based on observational data. This framework departs from traditional, individual-element modeling approaches, offering a more comprehensive and insightful method for studying emergent phenomena. The paper details the design of the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in simulating a simplified, yet representative, example of a complex system.

The core mechanism leverages the inherent quantum properties of particles to achieve more robust and adaptable pattern recognition. We present a novel approach that automatically identifies and analyzes resonant frequencies within a system, providing a foundation for enhanced stability. The algorithm's adaptability is achieved through a dynamically adjusting resonance threshold, allowing it to effectively identify and mitigate potential instability. This research contributes to the advancement of quantum system stability through the application of advanced pattern recognition techniques.

title: Real-World Case Studies in Trustworthy Computer Vision
abstract: Trustworthy computer vision (CV) is no longer a theoretical aspiration; it is a practical necessity wherever deep learning models are used in decision pipelines. Five domains illustrate this need: clinical imaging, autonomous vehicle perception, precision agriculture, satellite-based remote sensing, and biometric face recognition. In each domain a key trust dimension dominates discussion—fairness, robustness, on-device efficiency, cross-sensor domain adaptation, and privacy—yet these concerns often overlap in practice. This chapter examines each domain using empirical studies published between 2022 and 2025, highlighting major failure modes, attempted remedies, and remaining governance gaps. A comparative table and scored assessment across five trust axes provide a reference for practitioners, while a structured evaluation checklist supports pre-deployment and post-deployment audits. The chapter argues that trustworthiness must be integrated throughout the development and operational lifecycle.

title: Défis et jalons des calculateurs quantiques tolérants aux fautes
abstract: Dans cet article, nous faisons le point sur l’élaboration et l’usage potentiel des ordinateurs quantiques tolérants aux fautes capables de traiter de manière fiable des calculs complexes en surmontant les erreurs et le bruit inhérent aux systèmes quantiques. Dans un premier temps, les intérêts attendus en gains de performance par le calcul quantique sont évoqués ainsi que leurs limites à la fois théoriques et pratiques. Dans un second temps, la nécessaire correction d’erreurs quantiques est abordée. Cette dernière passe par l’encodage de l’information logique, que l’on souhaite protéger, sur un grand nombre de qubits physiques délocalisés afin d’avoir un qubit fiable. Tout en estimant qu’il faut au maximum mille qubits physiques pour obtenir un qubit logique fiable, nous soulignons la difficulté majeure que constitue le passage à l’échelle du nombre de qubits physiques pour résoudre des problèmes réels. Sont ensuite énoncées les différentes technologies de qubits ainsi que leurs enjeux. Puis est abordée la problématique du passage à l’échelle de manière modulaire par l’interconnexion de petits modules quantiques. Une quatrième partie mentionne les enjeux économiques et la coopétition avec les calculateurs classiques et l’IA. Tout en soulignant les progrès en cours et en observant la position française sur cinq voies technologiques, nous appelons aussi à la prudence au regard d’effets d’annonce.

title: Language-informed treatment recommendations in psychiatry: bridging the gap in individual predictability
abstract: Treatment recommendation systems in psychiatry perform suboptimally, largely due to low individual-level predictability from conventional clinical predictors. We argue that language captured through clinical interviews and electronic health records provides a rich, workflow-native substrate for estimating individualized treatment effects. We highlight opportunities for language-informed systems using modern language models and outline key challenges that must be addressed for safe and scalable deployment.

title: Explainable machine learning for breast mass characterization and malignancy risk stratification: multimodal integration of AI-derived structured digital breast tomosynthesis features and peripheral blood immune-inflammatory biomarkers
abstract: Background: Accurate discrimination between benign and malignant breast masses is essential for biopsy decisions and individualized management. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine-learning model integrating artificial intelligence (AI)-structured digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) mass features with peripheral blood immune-inflammatory indices. Methods: This retrospective study included 382 patients with 401 pathologically confirmed breast mass lesions (299 benign and 102 malignant) who underwent DBT before pathological examination. AI-structured DBT descriptors, clinical variables, and hematologic inflammatory indices were collected. Lesions were divided into training and testing cohorts using stratified random sampling at a 7:3 ratio. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression was used for feature selection, and five machine-learning models were trained. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), calibration, decision curve analysis, Brier score, and confusion matrix. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was used to interpret the final model, and predicted probabilities were used for descriptive risk stratification. Results: Logistic LASSO regression selected nine predictors: suspicious calcifications, irregular mass shape, age, long-axis diameter, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), short-axis diameter, oval mass shape, absence of calcifications, and obscured margin. In the testing cohort, the logistic regression model achieved the highest AUROC (0.884, 95% CI: 0.807-0.950), with an accuracy of 0.860, sensitivity of 0.806, specificity of 0.878, and negative predictive value of 0.929. SHAP analysis results indicate that suspicious calcifications, advanced age, irregular morphology, elevated NLR, and larger lesion size may be the primary factors contributing to the prediction of malignancy. The malignancy rate observed in this study ranged from 2.5% in the low-risk group to 67.6% in the high-risk group. Conclusion: The logistic regression (LR) model integrating AI-derived structured DBT features, clinical variables, and peripheral blood immune-inflammatory biomarkers demonstrated favorable performance for breast mass classification and malignancy risk stratification, with a test-set AUROC of 0.884. Prospective multicentre external validation is required.

title: РОБАСТНАЯ КЛАССИФИКАЦИЯ ЭМОЦИЙ В КИТАЙСКИХ РУКОПИСНЫХ ТЕКСТАХ В УСЛОВИЯХ ШУМА ОПТИЧЕСКОГО РАСПОЗНАВАНИЯ СИМВОЛОВ С ПРИМЕНЕНИЕМ ПРОФИЛЬНО- ОРИЕНТИРОВАННОЙ АУГМЕНТАЦИИ ДАННЫХ
abstract: В работе проверяется, что происходит с классификацией эмоций, когда на вход модели попадает не ручная транскрипция китайской рукописной строки, а результат PaddleOCR. Исходный корпус удобен для такой проверки: в нем есть изображения строк и их текстовые записи, но нет экспертной эмоциональной разметки. Поэтому сначала была зафиксирована слабая разметка, полученная по лексическим признакам и текстовому классификатору, а уже затем на ней обучались итоговые модели. Основным вариантом оставлена задача на семь эмоций. Одиннадцатиклассовая схема используется отдельно, как проверка поведения редких категорий. В режиме text-only лучшей оказалась RoBERTa: Accuracy 0,9304 и Macro-F1 0,8863. После замены ручных транскрипций OCR-выходом Macro-F1 снизилась до 0,8390. Для обучения с учетом таких ошибок был собран профиль фактических замен, удалений и вставок PaddleOCR; на его основе применялась профильно-ориентированная аугментация. В сквозном сценарии Macro-F1 выросла до 0,8636, а 95%-й доверительный интервал для разности не включал ноль. В одиннадцатиклассовом варианте Macro-F1 равна 0,8760, но редкие классы остаются ненадежными для самостоятельных выводов. Ручная проверка 480 объектов также показала, что псевдометки лишь частично совпадают с оценкой аннотатора. Поэтому приведенные метрики следует читать прежде всего как оценку устойчивости внутри выбранной слабой разметки, а не как точность относительно полноценного экспертного стандарта.

title: AI-powered enhancement of tourist experiences through personalization: a bibliometric study
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the transformative role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing personalization and efficiency in tourism. By analyzing current literature, it identifies key gaps and proposes actionable directions for advancing AI-driven innovation in the sector. Design/methodology/approach The research uses a bibliometric analysis of 185 peer-reviewed articles sourced from Web of Science and Scopus databases between 2014 and 2024. The study uses cooccurrence network analysis, supported by VOSviewer, to map thematic clusters and trends related to AI applications and personalization in tourism. Findings The keyword cooccurrence analysis revealed seven thematic clusters. Findings highlight growing scholarly interest in AI-driven personalization, chatbots, large language models and hybrid recommender systems, alongside increasing attention to ethical considerations such as algorithmic bias and data privacy. Originality/value This study contributes to the growing body of literature by presenting a research agenda focused on a critical perspective on AI adoption. It also contributes by explicitly linking ethical AI frameworks with user-centered innovation.

title: Segmentation of the aorta in 4D flow MRI using 4D convolutional kernels and learning from sparse annotations
abstract: Automated aortic segmentation in 4D flow MRI is essential for reproducible hemodynamic assessment but is limited by scarce dense annotations and high computational demands. We developed a fully automated 4D (3D+time) U-Net for segmenting the ascending aorta, arch, and proximal descending aorta, using a parameter-efficient hybrid 4D kernel to capture temporal context and sparse 4D labels derived from existing 2D expert contours and centerlines, thereby avoiding the need for dense 4D annotations. Training comprised 268 scans from 8 centers and 2 vendors, with evaluation on an internal test set (32 scans) and an external post-contrast set (30 scans; different site, protocol, and annotator), compared against frame-wise 3D networks and two semi-automatic references. Against time-resolved annotations, the 4D U-Net achieved Dice scores of 0.927 (internal) and 0.911 (external), versus 0.919/0.847 for the 3D U-Net, 0.893 for static PC-MRA, and 0.808 for registration-based propagation; differences were small in systole but pronounced in diastole. Agreement with expert contours for peak velocity, net flow, axial and circumferential wall shear stress, and diameters was excellent (ICC >=0.954 internal, >=0.980 external), while semi-automatic references performed worse. The method thus provides reproducible, time-resolved aortic segmentation for automated hemodynamic analysis and generalizes across multicenter, multivendor, and independent post-contrast data. The model is publicly available.

title: Rent-a-RAG: Embedding-Space Watermarks for Auditing Third-Party RAG
abstract: Third-party retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) marketplaces create a new auditing problem: data providers may license corpora to a RAG operator, yet later have no visibility into whether their documents are being reused without compensation. Auditing this misuse is difficult because the operator is non-cooperative, answers are paraphrased by the generator, and one response may combine evidence from many providers. We propose DirBucket, a provider-side semantic watermarking and black-box auditing framework for document-level reuse in multi-provider RAG. DirBucket watermarks documents by meaning-preserving paraphrases whose embeddings are biased toward provider-bucket secret directions, enabling detection from black-box answers while preserving retrieval utility. On a challenging benchmark that reflects mixed-provider reuse under black-box access, DirBucket is the only method that consistently achieves strong target detection with no non-target activation, detecting non-compliance in every audit within 23 audited answers on our primary benchmark. The watermark survives adversarial post-answer laundering, and none of the evaluated evasion strategies simultaneously defeats detection while preserving user-perceived answer quality. Detection transfers unchanged to a second benchmark built from real clinical, cyber-threat-intelligence, and legal provider corpora. These results suggest that embedding-space watermarking can make document reuse in third-party RAG statistically auditable.

title: A Bi-directional multi-solution scalable Grover search Algorithm
abstract: Abstract Grover’s search algorithms, including various partial Grover searches (PGS), experience scaling problems when multiple solutions are sought, as the number of iterations increases with the number of solutions or marked states, making implementation more computationally expensive. Inspired by recent PGS algorithms for multi-solution searchers, this article proposes a scalable Grover quantum search algorithm, referred to as Bi-directional Multi-solution scalable Grover Search (BMGS), to efficiently search for an arbitrary number of solutions from an unstructured database. We introduced a novel multi-segment bidirectional search tactic with PGS across multiple equal segments of each state, starting from an initial state and multiple marked states in parallel, obviating the need for merge operations. We have shown in this work that for each solution our novel approach requires at most $$\sqrt{\mathcal {N}}\left( 1- \sqrt{\frac{1}{b^{\lfloor \frac{r}{dk}\rfloor }}}\right) $$ N 1 - 1 b ⌊ r dk ⌋ iterations (here, $$\mathcal {N}=2^r$$ N = 2 r elements, $$k=\log _2 b$$ k = log 2 b , d is the number of equal segments on r qubits, and b is the branching factor). Our proposed BMGS algorithm is benchmarked against state-of-the-art Depth-First Grover Search (DFGS) and PGS implementations for an arbitrary number of solutions, ranging from 2 to 20 qubits, as a proof of concept. We also show that our BMGS requires fewer iterations for shallow quantum circuits and achieves an optimal $$\mathcal {O}$$ O ( $$\sqrt{s\mathcal {N}}$$ s N ) average complexity for s solutions, when $$dk < r$$ d k < r . The Qiskit Python implementation of the proposed BMGS algorithm is available on GitHub ( https://github.com/hafeezzwiz21/Multi-Solution-DFGS-BMGS ).

title: Quantum Information Entropy Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: Quantum information is a fundamental resource for quantum computation and information processing. Its inherent fragility makes accurate representation and manipulation challenging. This paper proposes a dynamic algorithm for adjusting the entropy of quantum information, aiming to enhance the accuracy of quantum simulations and data analysis. We introduce a novel framework based on the principle that quantum information entropy, when manipulated dynamically, can subtly shift the system's state, thereby improving the fidelity of computations. This approach directly addresses limitations of current entropy estimation techniques by incorporating a real-time, adaptive adjustment mechanism. The algorithm's efficacy will be demonstrated through illustrative examples and a focused analysis of its impact on simulation accuracy.

title: ##拓扑拓扑的量子计算验证
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing verification framework predicated on topological quantum computing principles. The framework leverages the inherent robustness of topological structures to rigorously validate quantum algorithms, enhancing their reliability and minimizing errors. We propose a method for constructing and validating quantum algorithms through the examination of their topological properties, allowing for the detection of subtle errors that classical verification methods often miss. This approach offers a fundamentally different approach to quantum verification, focusing on the underlying structure of the quantum system rather than relying on computationally expensive classical analysis. The paper details the core mechanism of this framework, outlining the steps involved in building, validating, and interpreting the resulting topological structure. The potential benefits of this method include improved algorithm robustness, reduced error rates, and a deeper understanding of quantum system behavior. Finally, we discuss the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Wave Function Collapse for Material Synthesis
abstract: Quantum-enhanced wave function collapse offers a revolutionary approach to material synthesis, addressing the limitations of current methods characterized by inefficiency and unpredictability. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum superposition to accelerate and refine the collapse of wave functions, ultimately leading to improved material purity and control. We detail the core mechanism of this approach, focusing on the application of quantum algorithms to rapidly explore a vast conformational space of potential material configurations. The research highlights the significant advantages over conventional methods, emphasizing the potential for achieving unprecedented levels of precision and control in material design. The core claim is that a carefully designed quantum algorithm can significantly enhance the probability of obtaining desired material states.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Theory with Adaptive Parameterization
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos theory aims to overcome the limitations of static parameterizations by dynamically adjusting model parameters based on observed data. This paper explores a novel quantum algorithm designed to achieve this, utilizing a quantum process to iteratively refine chaos model parameters, resulting in enhanced predictive accuracy. The core mechanism involves quantum evolution of the chaos model, continuously adapting to new data points. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in chaos theory, moving beyond static representations and embracing adaptive, data-driven approaches. The study delves into the theoretical foundations and experimental validation of this quantum-enhanced algorithm, demonstrating its ability to improve predictive performance in a simulated environment.

title: Quantum Noise Modeling and Suppression in Quantum Sensors
abstract: Quantum sensors represent a revolutionary technology with the potential to surpass the limits of classical sensors across a wide range of applications, including precision measurement, navigation, and medical diagnostics. However, the realization of this potential is significantly hindered by the pervasive presence of noise. This work addresses the critical need for accurate noise modeling and effective suppression techniques within quantum sensors. We introduce a novel noise model that incorporates both thermal and coherent noise sources, explicitly accounting for the quantum mechanical nature of these sensors. This model is then utilized to design and analyze various noise suppression strategies, including feedback control algorithms and advanced filtering methods. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for improved sensor design and operation, ultimately driving advancements in quantum sensing technology. The core claim of this work is that precise noise modeling and effective suppression techniques are paramount for enhancing the precision of quantum sensors. This is achieved through the establishment of a new noise model and the subsequent design of suppression techniques such as feedback control and filtering. The novelty lies in the detailed and accurate representation of noise sources within the quantum sensor system.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Modeling Causal Inference
abstract: This paper explores the application of probabilistic programming languages to the field of causal inference. Traditional methods for causal modeling often rely on complex assumptions and can be difficult to interpret and modify. Probabilistic programming offers a more natural and flexible approach, allowing researchers to directly represent causal relationships using probabilistic models. We propose a framework for defining causal models, incorporating observational data and simulated interventions. The core of this approach involves utilizing inference algorithms to estimate causal effects and perform hypothesis testing. This framework demonstrates a significant advancement over existing techniques by providing a more intuitive and adaptable method for understanding and reasoning about causality. We outline the key components of this framework, focusing on model specification, data integration, and inference techniques. The ultimate goal is to provide a robust and accessible tool for causal discovery and analysis.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Symbolic Regression
abstract: Symbolic regression aims to discover mathematical expressions that accurately represent a given dataset. Traditional methods often struggle with complex datasets and can be computationally expensive. This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to the problem of symbolic regression. We propose representing symbolic expressions as graphs, where nodes represent variables and operators, and edges represent mathematical relationships. A GNN is then trained to learn the optimal graph structure, effectively learning the underlying mathematical function directly from the data. The core claim is that GNNs offer a viable alternative to traditional symbolic regression, potentially overcoming its limitations by leveraging the ability of GNNs to learn complex, non-linear relationships. We detail the graph representation, the GNN architecture, and the training process. Experimental results, though not presented through formal experimentation due to the nature of this exploration, illustrate the potential of this approach. The proposed method demonstrates the ability to learn complex expressions, suggesting a promising direction for future research in automated mathematical discovery.

title: Multi-Agent Simulation of Complex Social Systems using Agent-Based Modeling with Differential Privacy
abstract: Agent-based models (ABMs) have emerged as a powerful tool for simulating and understanding complex social systems, ranging from urban dynamics to disease propagation. However, traditional ABMs often rely on detailed data, including potentially sensitive individual-level information, which can lead to data leakage and privacy violations during simulation and analysis. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates ABMs with differential privacy (DP) to address this challenge. The framework allows for the creation of realistic and robust social system simulations while safeguarding the privacy of agent behaviors. We introduce a mechanism where differential privacy is applied to the simulation data, obfuscating individual agent actions and preventing the inference of sensitive information. The core claim of this work is that combining ABMs with DP provides a viable solution for simulating complex social systems securely. We detail the key components of the framework and discuss its potential applications.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of non-linear modal geometry as a novel approach to quantum computing verification, aiming to enhance algorithm performance and facilitate more efficient quantum data processing. We propose a new geometric framework predicated on quantum entanglement to accelerate computational processes and leverage entanglement effects for quantum circuit analysis. The core mechanism centers on designing a modal geometry that intrinsically exploits entanglement, thereby providing a robust and efficient verification methodology. This research explores the creation of a quantum algorithm verification framework, incorporating the geometric principles to provide a superior validation process. The study highlights the benefits of this approach in optimizing quantum computation, and represents a promising step towards more reliable and scalable quantum systems.
